Driving transparency in ESG 
governance
Vedanta places strong emphasis on transparency and responsible disclosure as core pillars of effective ESG governance. The company continuously monitors the evolving global landscape of corporate governance standards, particularly in the ESG domain, incorporating insights from national and international regulations, industry frameworks, investor expectations, and peer benchmarking. These insights inform enhancements to internal policies and practices, which are implemented following Board approval. Vedanta also actively evaluates emerging expectations around ESG-linked performance management and compensation and has integrated climate-related parameters into the evaluation criteria of its Long-Term Incentive Programmes, strengthening accountability and alignment with sustainability priorities.The company continues to strengthen its internal governance and monitoring mechanisms in response to evolving standards and stakeholder expectations. This includes periodic refinement of the Vedanta Sustainability Assurance Process (VSAP), which supports robust oversight of ESG performance across business units and ensures that sustainability practices are systematically embedded into operations.
Transparency and information 
sharing remain central to stakeholder engagement. Vedanta publishes a comprehensive suite of ESG disclosures, including the Annual Integrated Report, Sustainability Report, TCFD Climate Report, and Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report (BRSR). These disclosures are aligned with internationally recognised frameworks such as the Global Reporting Initiative (GRI), Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD), and the Integrated Reporting Framework, ensuring consistency, credibility, and comparability. The publication of Vedanta’s 18
th Sustainability 
Report reflects sustained progress in integrating sustainability into business strategy and governance.
The strength of these disclosures, 
combined with continuous improvements in governance practices and ESG performance, has led to upgraded ratings from multiple independent agencies. V-Aspire: Talent Search Initiative
We launched V-Aspire, our flagship 
internal talent discovery initiative, under the leadership of Ms Priya Hebbar. The programme identifies and nurtures the next generation of high-potential leaders through tailored development opportunities, challenging assignments and future-focussed exposure.
The selection process was designed 
with global HR consultants and included AI-enabled interviews, business simulations and psychometric tools. Candidates were shortlisted through a multi-stage evaluation based on performance, potential and pedigree. Finalists were assessed by a leadership panel comprising internal and external industry experts.
The identified talent will undergo 
structured developmental interventions in the coming year, strengthening our future-ready leadership cadre.
Talent Mobility and Internal  
Job Posting
We see talent mobility as a strategic 
lever for building leadership capability. Our approach is rooted in leadership from within, and we encourage employees to gain diverse exposure across roles, businesses and geographies.
Our Internal Job Posting (IJP) process 
provides transparent, merit-based access to career opportunities. It empowers employees to take ownership of their growth while supporting business continuity and performance delivery. We also take a long-term view of potential, often backing people when they are partly ready for a role, as stretch assignments build confidence, capability and leadership depth.Our career philosophy, expressed as ‘3 Roles, 3 Businesses, 3 Locations’, provides holistic exposure through structured role movements and stretch opportunities. This builds a Group-wide perspective and prepares high-potential talent for critical leadership positions. As a result, most roles across Vedanta are filled internally, while external hiring is focussed on niche skills, deep domain expertise and select leadership roles requiring specialised capabilities.
We also follow a structured job 
rotation practice, guided by clear policies and strong governance. Employees are encouraged to take up new roles at periodic intervals, supporting continuous learning, succession planning and business continuity.
ACT -UP: Business and Technical
The Accelerated Competency Tracking and Upgradation Process (ACT-UP) is a strategic talent development programme that identifies and prepares high-potential employees for key roles. Conducted with leading external consultants, the programme uses aspiration questionnaires, case studies, online personality profiling and group assignments.We have introduced External Expert Panels to bring independent, outside-in perspectives to CXO hiring. These panels include seasoned industry leaders who support leadership assessment through global insight, functional depth and unbiased judgement.
The panels help us reduce 
unconscious bias, strengthen decision-making and assess candidates across strategic, behavioural and cultural dimensions. This approach brings greater balance, rigour and impartiality to critical leadership appointments.

Our Governance Framework
Our governance framework is anchored in our core values of Trust, Entrepreneurship, Innovation, Excellence, Integrity, Respect 
and Care. These values guide our vision, strategic mission and commitment to sustainable growth. The framework enables us to align business performance with accountability, stakeholder expectations and long-term value creation across our diversified natural resources portfolio.
Corporate Governance 
Philosophy
Good governance defines our long-
term value creation philosophy. We see purpose-led governance and ethics-driven conduct as essential to our ambition of building India’s largest diversified natural resources conglomerate and positioning ourselves among the most sustainable organisations globally.
Our governance ethos reflects a 
dual operating approach. Each entity within the Group has its own management systems and operational responsibilities, while the Group functions cohesively through a shared purpose and common governance standards. This approach helps us combine entrepreneurial agility with institutional discipline.
We view responsible operations 
as our fiduciary duty as trustees of multiple capitals: financial, manufactured, intellectual, human, social and relationship, and natural. This stewardship guides the way we manage resources, execute our integrated value chain and deliver consistent value for stakeholders.
An engaged and informed Board 
leads this governance philosophy. The Board brings diverse expertise,

Market Review
Economic Outlook
The year 2025-26 was marked by moderate 
and uneven global economic growth, as economies adjusted to increased trade protectionism, financial market volatility, and ongoing geopolitical uncertainties. While inflation eased and recession risks declined, structural challenges continued to shape the global outlook.
2025 – The Year of Uncertainty
The last fiscal started with President Donald Trump’s sweeping "Liberation Day" tariffs announcements in April 2025 introducing a baseline 10% global tariff alongside specific "reciprocal" tariffs scaling up to 50% for countries with high trade surpluses. This was followed by a series of negotiations, multiple changes in tariff rates and heightened trade tensions among the countries as they attempted to make trade deals with the US to achieve a favourable tariff structure. However, in February 2026, the US Supreme Court ruled the initial tariffs illegal, stating that the emergency powers cited under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA) did not permit the President to bypass Congress to regulate international commerce. In response to the Supreme Court's decision, the US administration instituted a 10% blanket global tariff under Section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974, which was again ruled out by the U.S. Court of International Trade (CIT) in May 2026.
The year was marked by increased number of 
conflicts amidst failed attempts to end Russia-Ukraine war and fragile ceasefire in Gaza. New frontier opened in Middle East when the US, Israel and Iran engaged into the 12-Day War intensive conflict in June 2025 involving Israeli strikes on Iranian military and nuclear sites, followed by direct U.S. intervention.
Towards the end of the fiscal year, the fierce war 
broke out in Middle East between Iran and the US-Israel which rattled global energy market.
All these things culminated in heightened 
uncertainty regarding global business environment which is reflected in World Uncertainty Index which touched all-time high in September 2025, dwarfing the previous spikes like Covid-19 pandemic of 2020 or Global Financial Crisis of 2008.Resilient Global Economy
Despite all the odds, global economy expanded by 3.4% in 2025, indicating stable but modest expansion. Growth remained strong in emerging economies which grew by 4.4%, but moderate in advanced economies with 1.9% rise in 2025. The United States maintained steady growth of 2.1% driven by consumption and technology investment. China managed to achieve the target 5% growth, supported by policy measures but constrained by real estate issues. India remained one of the fastest-growing major economies at 7.6%. Euro Area saw slower growth of 1.4% due to structural weaknesses. Overall, global growth was resilient but remained below long-term averages.
Pace of decline in inflation slowed down in 2025 and global 
inflation largely remained steady. Inflation in the US remained above target level while that in India and EU started moving up during Q4 of FY 2025-26. As a result, the Federal Reserve kept its benchmark interest rate unchanged at 3.50–3.75% during meetings in January, March, and April in 2026 while the European Central Bank did not reduce interest rates after June 2025.
Global manufacturing in 2025 experienced a slow but steady 
recovery, characterised by moderate output growth. Global manufacturing PMI consistently remained in expansionary zone since August 2025 and reached 52.6 in April 2026 - marking a 49-month high and signalling a strengthened expansion in worldwide manufacturing output despite rising geopolitical risks. Global trade in 2025 reached a record high of US$ 34.65 trillion in total value, a 7% increase over 2024. Growth was driven by strong demand for electronics and AI-related hardware. However, sustenance of such positive developments are overshadowed by the ongoing war between Iran and the combined forces of US and Israel.

Middle East Crisis Risks Global Growth 
Prospect
The US-Iran war which started since 28 February 2026 has 
emerged as a major geopolitical shock with wide-ranging consequences for the global economy. Given the strategic importance of the Middle East in global energy supply and trade routes, the conflict has affected growth, inflation, trade, and financial stability worldwide.
The most immediate impact has been a sharp rise in global 
oil prices. The conflict disrupted the Strait of Hormuz, through which about 20% of global oil supply flows. Oil prices surged above US$ 100 per barrel in some phases. Rising oil and commodity prices have led to global inflation pressures. Many economies face the risk of imported inflation due to energy dependence. Higher cost of living (fuel, food, utilities), reduced purchasing power, pressure on low-income households.
Disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz have 
impacted several commodity markets, affecting both energy and related sectors. The Gulf region, which accounts for about 8% of global aluminium supply, is also affected. Roughly 5 million tonnes are shipped annually through the Strait from countries like Bahrain, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, and the UAE, impacting construction, manufacturing, and energy technologies.
Fertiliser supply is especially vulnerable, with over 30% 
of global urea trade and around 20% of ammonia and phosphate shipments passing through the Strait. This raises concerns for food prices and security. There are also indirect energy implications, as some countries rely on imported LNG to power fertiliser production.
In addition, nearly half of global seaborne sulphur trade 
moves through this route. Sulphuric acid derived from it is essential for fertilisers, chemicals, petroleum refining, and processing key minerals such as copper, nickel, and zinc.
Oil and gas prices almost doubled and aluminium price 
also jumped due to supply disruption in Q4. While copper 
and silver prices reached all-time high earlier in the quarter, they retreated in the later part of the quarter due to profit booking, strengthening US dollar, fear of interest rate hike and concern of adverse impact of manufacturing.
The United States and Iran agreed to a fragile, two-week 
ceasefire on 8 April 2026, following which oil and gas prices pulled back. However, the ceasefire is currently in a state of tension following the failure of high-stakes negotiations. Resumption of the war and continuation of that may keep the commodity market extremely volatile.
Global Economic Outlook
The demand outlook has weakened as the conflict in the Middle East has disrupted fuel supplies, which will take time to recover once the Strait of Hormuz is fully reopened. But even that will not lead to a speedy return to normal as oil and gas production facilities and infrastructure have been damaged. As such, the fallout from the conflict could be felt for many months as it will take time for other producers to increase production to make up for the lasting losses in incurred by the affected Middle Eastern countries.
Central banks face a policy dilemma as inflation is likely to 
rise due to oil shocks while growth slowing due to economic uncertainty. This could delay interest rate cuts and possible tightening if inflation persists. This creates risks of stagflation which is a condition of low growth and high inflation, slower growth, and financial instability.
World industrial production growth for 2026 has been 
revised down from 3.1% to 2.5% as a result of the fallout of the conflict. With Asia and Europe highly dependent on Middle East oil and gas, higher-for-longer energy prices, energy rationing and the inflationary implications of these, means that there is a risk that broader markets turn bearish and that weighs on sentiment in the base metals.In the baseline outlook by IMF, global growth is expected to reach 3.1% in 2026 and 3.2% in 2027. This represents a slowdown from the roughly 3.4% pace observed in 2024-25, with growth stabilising at a similarly lower rate over the medium term – well below the historical average of 3.7% recorded between 2000 and 2019. Compared with the January 2026 WEO Update, the 2026 forecast has been revised down by 0.2 percentage points, while the 2027 projection remains unchanged. Meanwhile, global headline inflation is projected to rise to 4.4% in 2026 before easing to 3.7% in 2027, with both figures revised upward.
In a downside scenario characterised by larger and more 
sustained increases in energy prices, global growth would weaken further to 2.5% in 2026, while inflation would climb to 5.4%. Under a more severe scenario involving greater damage to energy infrastructure in the conflict-affected region, the consequences would intensify: global growth would fall to around 2% in 2026, and headline inflation would exceed 6% by 2027. Emerging market and developing economies would bear a disproportionately larger burden, experiencing impacts nearly twice as severe as those faced by advanced economies.
China
China's economy in 2025 achieved 5% growth, driven by robust manufacturing and exports despite persistent deflationary pressures, a prolonged property slump, and weak domestic demand.
In industrial sector, high-tech manufacturing outpaced the 
overall growth rate, with significant expansion in sectors like civil drones, embedded intelligence, and industrial robots. Fixed assets investments (FAI) registered a negative growth of 3.8% in 2025 – first time since 1989, mainly dragged down by 17% degrowth in investment in real estate sector. China's "anti-involution" drive to curb "race-to-the-bottom" competition, overcapacity, and destructive price wars, particularly in manufacturing also severely impacted FAI in manufacturing which could merely grew by 0.6% in 2025. Depressive situation in property market extended in 2025 as well with 12.6% decline in building sold which calls for more structured and extended policy support from the Chinese government.
In March 2026, China adopted 15
th Five-Year Plan 
(2026-2030) which focusses on technological self-reliance, 
"new quality productive forces," and security-driven development. It sets a pragmatic 2026 GDP growth target of 4.5-5.0%. This shift prioritises high-quality development, technological self-reliance (AI, quantum computing), and service-sector growth over rapid speed. China has also stepped up efforts to launch major projects and boost investment in new types of infrastructure. The plan aims to manage domestic structural adjustments and weak demand, marking the lowest target in decades.
IMF has projected China’s GDP growth to decelerate to 4.4% 
in 2026 and 4% in 2027 from 5% in 2025 due to ongoing structural issues, specifically a prolonged property sector downturn, weak domestic consumption, an ageing labour force, and mounting trade tensions.

USA
The U.S. economy in 2025 showed steady and broad-
based growth – growing by 2.1%. This was driven mainly by strong consumer spending, a robust labour market, and AI-led technological investment. Despite challenges from high interest rates and global risks, the economy remained resilient and one of the strongest among advanced nations. Household consumption remained the largest driver of GDP , supported by strong labour market, rising wages and excess savings from previous years. US unemployment rate remained at 4.3% by the end of April 2026. But inflation rate jumped to 3.8% in April from 2.4% during January and February 2026 from rising energy cost.
US Fed adopted a cautious, data-dependent approach to 
interest rates in 2026, balancing inflation risks with concerns about economic growth due to ongoing Middle East war and rising fuel cost. As of early 2026, the Fed has kept the federal funds rate at 3.50%–3.75%. The Fed’s “dot plot” indicates only one rate cut in 2026 of 25 basis points, indicating a cautious "higher-for-longer" stance.
In February 2026, the U.S. Supreme Court ruled that 
President Trump's tariffs, imposed under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA), were unlawful, ruling that only Congress has the authority to set import taxes. However, Donald Trump immediately activated Section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974, which allows for a temporary 15% general tariff to handle balance-of-payments issues. A 10% general tariff was subsequently slated to take effect by 24 February 2026, which is temporary (150 days) without Congressional approval.
The US economy is likely to be least affected by the Middle 
East war. IMF expects US GDP to grow by 2.3% in 2026 and 2.1% in 2027.European Union
The European Union's real GDP increased by 1.6% in 2025. 
This represented an acceleration from the 1.2% growth recorded in 2024. Economic performance varied significantly across the bloc, with smaller and island nations generally outpacing larger economies. Domestic demand remained a primary driver, supported by a resilient labour market and real wage increases as inflation cooled. Inflation stabilised around 2.1% for the year, significantly lower than previous peaks, which helped restore consumer purchasing power. As a result, ECB kept interest rates unchanged at 2.15% since June 2025. Manufacturing activities considerably improved as reflected in PMI reading which moved up to 52 in April 2026.
However, the war in the Middle East has brought renewed 
uncertainty and the economic outlook is clouded again. Disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, a key route for global oil and liquefied natural gas (LNG) trade. The baseline projections of IMF foresee annual real GDP growth of 1.3% in 2026 and 1.4% in 2027 and gas price-led cost push weighs on cost of living.
India
India’s economy stayed resilient in 2025-26, with real GDP growth of 7.6% under the Second Advance Estimates (base year 2022-23). Growth was mainly driven by strong private consumption and fixed investment, while net external demand remained weak. On the supply side, real GVA rose 7.7%, supported by robust services and manufacturing.
However, the ongoing conflict has increased volatility in 
global energy and commodity prices, creating uncertainty for the near-term growth and inflation outlook of India. Roughly 45% of crude oil and 60% of natural gas imports of India originate from the Middle East, making India’s energy security highly vulnerable to regional conflicts and shipping disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz. Higher global energy costs have pushed up prices of fuels like premium petrol, LPG, and industrial diesel.
The Indian rupee hit an all-time low of 95.75 against the US 
Dollar on 14 May 2026, driven by intense pressures from the Middle East conflict, surging oil prices, and significant foreign capital outflows.
Indian domestic industries also initially experienced 
disruptions due to constrained availability of natural gas, as the Indian government had prioritised natural gas and LPG allocation to households and transport over industrial users following supply disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz. Subsequently, government gradually increased the allocation of bulk non-domestic LPG to industrial sectors closure to their pre-March 2026 consumption levels.
The Government of India has launched several emergency 
measures to support domestic industries and exporters facing disruptions due to the US-Iran conflict and related volatility in West Asia.
 •The RELIEF Scheme: The Ministry of Commerce and 
Industry introduced the ` 497 crore RELIEF (Resilience & 
Logistics Intervention for Export Facilitation) scheme to mitigate rising freight and insurance costs for exporters targeting 10 West Asian countries. It assists exporters facing high freight costs, rising insurance premiums, and logistics delays in West Asia, covering regions like the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, and expanding to include Egypt and Jordan.
 –Risk Coverage: ECGC Ltd. (Formerly Export Credit Guarantee Corporation of India Ltd.) offers up to 100% risk coverage over and above the existing ECGC cover for existing policies from 14 February 2026 till 15 March 2026 and 95% for new shipments between 14 February and 15 June 2026, keeping premiums at pre-conflict rates.
 –MSME Support: Provides up to 50% reimbursement (capped at ` 50 lakhs) for extraordinary shipping/insurance surcharges.
 •Restoration of Duty Benefits: Government fully restored RoDTEP (Remission of Duties and Taxes on Exported Products) rates and value caps till  30 September 2026 for the benefit of exporters, reversing a February reduction of 50%.
 •Logistical Support: Govt launched US$ 1.5 billion Bharat Maritime Insurance Pool with sovereign guarantee to secure shipping risks.
Looking ahead to 2026-27, high energy and commodity prices and potential supply disruptions (e.g., Strait of Hormuz) may weigh on production. Global financial volatility and trade disruptions could also impact growth, especially exports due to higher shipping and insurance costs. However, strong services momentum, GST rationalisation, rising manufacturing capacity use, and healthy corporate and financial balance sheets should support demand. With government initiatives to boost domestic manufacturing, GDP growth is projected at 6.9% (Q1: 6.8%, Q2: 6.7%, Q3: 7.0%, Q4: 7.2%) by RBI, higher than 6.5% projected by IMF. Risks remain from prolonged conflict, wider geopolitical tensions, energy infrastructure damage, and weather shocks.
Taking these factors into account, CPI inflation for 2026-27 
is projected at 4.6% (Q1: 4.0%, Q2: 4.4%, Q3: 5.2%, Q4: 4.7%). Upside risks remain due to persistently high energy prices from the West Asia conflict and potential El Niño conditions that could affect the southwest monsoon.

Segment Review
Aluminium
Market Overview
The aluminium market on the 
LME witnessed considerable price fluctuations in FY 2025-26. In April 2025, aluminium prices were US$ 2,381 per tonne, rising to US$ 2,600/t levels in July due to 50% tariffs imposed by USA in June 2025. LME maintained steady uptrend till January 2026 rising to ~3,150/t levels due to various factors; China’s production nearing the production cap of 45 MTPA, weakening of US Dollar, & frequent variations in tariffs from USA. The middle east conflict led smelter shutdowns propelled LME prices to multi-year highs of ~3,400 US$/t during March.
In CY 2025, global primary 
aluminium production was ~1.1% up from last year and around 73.8 million tonnes. The demand was also around at the same level with deficit balance of ~0.2 million. In the world excluding China, both production and consumption were at similar levels as per last year. China’s production increased in CY 2025 was 44.2 MTPA. In India, the demand surged by ~10% to around 6 million tonnes in FY 2025-26.Market Outlook
The global demand for aluminium is anticipated to increase at a CAGR of ~2.5% from 2025 to 2030. Decarbonisation initiatives and a transition away from fossil fuels in the transportation sector will see an increase in aluminium consumption up to ~32 million tonnes by 2030. The demand for renewable energy will drive an increased demand for aluminium for solar panel manufacturing, transmission & distribution and the replacement of existing copper wiring in power distribution systems.
China, the world's largest 
aluminium consumer, shows promising signs of continued domestic consumption growth. However, its long-term success hinges on sustained growth in the transportation sector and modest recovery of the building & construction industry. For the Rest of the World, 2026 is 
expected to experience volatile market due to macroeconomic conditions like tariffs from USA, and geopolitical situations impacting trade flow & fuel and commodity prices and decrease in global production capacity due to expected shutdown of South32 Aluminium Smelter (Mozal) from March 2026.
Meanwhile, India stands out 
with its robust domestic demand outlook of more than 8% growth for FY 2026-27. Key sectors like electrical industry, automotive, and anticipated growth in renewables, defence and aerospace will continue to drive aluminium consumption in the country.
Products and Customers
Vedanta is India’s largest primary aluminium producer with an annual capacity of ~2.4 million tonnes. The Company’s product portfolio includes aluminium ingots, primary foundry alloys, wire rods, billets, and rolled products which cater to varied industries globally such as energy, transportation, construction and packaging, aerospace and defence, among others. It has achieved domestic market share of 46%.
In line with the evolving market 
needs and the focus on value creation through expanding margins, the Company has been steadily increasing its value-added product (VAP) share in the portfolio which currently accounts for ~60% of its total global aluminium sales and targeting ~90%.

High Carbon 
Ferro Chrome
Market Overview
High Carbon Ferro Chrome 
(HCFC) is pivotal to the global stainless-steel industry, enhancing its non-corrosive, durable, and temperature-resistant qualities. Over 85% of HCFC production is dedicated to stainless steel manufacturing, indicating that a flourishing stainless-steel sector is a bellwether for strong HCFC demand.
Asia, with China at the 
helm, dominates the HCFC landscape, accounting for 85% of consumption and holding substantial chromite ore reserves, the essential raw material. Although South Africa is the premier chromite ore supplier worldwide, China’s leadership in HCFC production positions it as a dominant force in shaping global market dynamics and pricing structures.India is playing a significant role in the HCFC market, securing the position as the world’s fourth-largest producer with an output of ~1.2 million tonnes in CY 2025. India’s HCFC market is characterised by an export orientation, with ~55% of its production being exported.
In Q4 FY 2025-26, Ferro chrome 
prices peaked at ` 1,24,000/T highest levels since September 2023. Demand in Q1 FY 2026-27 is primarily driven by exports which is supported by the exchange rate making exports much more lucrative as the domestic demand is expected to pick up gradually trailing the robust stainless steel prices.
Market Drivers
With India’s solid domestic market and the anticipated global upswing in stainless steel production, the outlook for HCFC is optimistic. With increasing infrastructure initiatives in developing nations and an expected resurgence in demand from China, stainless steel production is projected to grow steadily by 4-5% in the upcoming year. This growth trajectory is set to catalyse HCFC demand worldwide, with production forecasts suggesting an increase of 3-4%.
India, however, is on track to 
surpass the global growth rate, emerging as the fastest-expanding market for both stainless steel and HCFC production. The projected 7-8% growth in Stainless Steel sector is propelled by the Indian government’s substantial investment in infrastructure development. Moreover, India’s per capita consumption of stainless steel is poised for a significant uptick, mirroring the expanding domestic HCFC market.
Company Overview
Ferro Alloys Corporation (FACOR) stands out in the domestic HCFC sector, ranking as the fourth-largest supplier amidst a predominantly export-oriented industry. In FY 2025-26, FACOR channelled almost all of its HCFC production to meet the needs of domestic stainless steel and alloy steel manufacturers.
Getting future-ready along 
with expansion, FACOR is also strategically augmenting its Value-Added Products (VAP) portfolio, thereby securing a competitive edge to serve specialised markets in Europe and South Korea. Looking forward to FY 2026-27, FACOR’s strategy is geared towards amplifying production volumes and expanding its market presence, both domestically and globally.
At our Ferroalloy business, our 
strategic emphasis remains on capacity expansion, prioritising domestic market, VAP development, and strategic international market expansion. We are ideally positioned to thrive in this dynamic market landscape.
Oil
Global Oil Market Overview
In 2025, the global oil supply 
experienced moderate growth, primarily driven by both non-OPEC nations such as the United States (+0.76 Mb/d), Brazil (+0.37 Mb/d), Canada (+0.26 Mb/d), Kazakhstan (+0.27 Mb/d), China, and OPEC nations like Saudi Arabia (+0.49 Mb/d), UAE and Venezuela. Global oil demand also saw an upward trend, increasing by approximately 1.14 Mb/d. Sustained economic growth across Asia, driven by continued expansion in China, India, and other non-OECD countries, has been the primary catalyst for rising oil demand, fuelled largely by increasing transportation and industrial fuel consumption in these regions.
India's oil demand in 2025 
rose to 5.65 Mb/d (+0.1 Mb/d). It maintained strong growth driven by robust private consumption following GST reductions and sustained government spending. Monetary easing through rate cuts further supported growth momentum, though labour market pressures persisted.Crude oil prices in 2025 averaged US$ 69.1 per barrel, marking a 14.5% decline from 2024. Monthly prices trended broadly downwards from US$ 79.2 in January to US$ 62.7 by year end, with a brief spike in June–July due to the US Iran conflict. The overall decline was driven by the unwinding of OPEC+ voluntary cuts and abundant supply from outside the group causing a supply glut. OPEC+ began reversing the reductions made in 2023 by fully restoring 2.2 mb/d of output by September and partially rolling back the remaining 1.65 mb/d later in the year. Despite this oversupply, geo-political events like Middle East conflict led to sudden spike in crude oil price to over US$ 100/bbl since March 2026.
Market Drivers
OPEC forecasts global oil demand will grow by 1.4 Mb/d to reach 106.5 Mb/d in 2026. This increase will be driven by strong air travel demand, greater road mobility, including on-road diesel and trucking, and robust industrial, construction, and agricultural activities, particularly in non-OECD nations. Non-OECD production is expected to rise by 0.4 Mb/d in 2026, with growth led by the Latin American region (+0.4 Mb/d). Geopolitical factors, including the ongoing Middle East conflict and trade tariffs, could significantly impact global oil supply.
Brent crude oil prices have surged 
sharply following the outbreak of military conflict in the Middle East, rising more than 50% since the start of 2026. The U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA) projects that Brent will average around US$ 79 per barrel in 2026, as the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz temporarily reduces Middle Eastern oil production. Prices are expected to remain elevated through the second quarter of 2026, before easing below US$ 80 per barrel in the third quarter as production gradually resumes with the reopening of the Strait.
Manufacturing, business activity, 
air travel, and road mobility are expected to stay steady, while government initiatives such as Make in India, GST reforms, and the PMUY scheme will boost local demand. Strong GDP growth is also likely to sustain internal combustion engine vehicle sales amid slow EV penetration, pointing to a positive near-term outlook for oil product demand which is forecast to increase by 0.23 Mb/d to 5.9 Mb/d in 2026.
Products and Customers
Cairn Oil & Gas, is one of the largest private oil and gas exploration and production companies in the country, has gross proven and probable reserves and resources of 1,321 million barrels of oil equivalent (mmboe). The company’s crude oil is sold to both public and private refineries, while its natural gas is consumed by the city gas distribution, fertiliser, and other industrial sectors in India.
In FY 2025-26, 100% of the 
company’s crude oil and natural gas production was sold within India, in accordance with government regulations.

Power Sector
Demand and Supply
India's power sector witnessed 
significant advancements in FY 2025-26, highlighted by a record peak power demand of 245 GW, met with resilience and improved energy infrastructure. India's power sector has shown strong growth, with electricity generation 1,830 billion units in FY 2024-25 and 1,848 billion units in FY 2025-26, witnessing 1% Y-o-Y growth. Capacity additions were robust at 12%, bringing total installed capacity to 533 GW in FY 2025-26 compared to 475 GW in FY 2024-25. Notable strides were made in renewable energy, with an additional 55 GW capacity added in FY 2025-26, and 7G W coal-based plant capacity addition in same period to meet rising demand. As per CEA, India is projected to witness coal (including lignite) installed capacity requirement of 291 GW by FY 2031-32 to meet round the clock power demand.With initiatives like universal electrification, improved rural power availability, and enhanced energy conservation efforts, India is on a robust path to becoming a global energy leader.
Market drivers
India's power sector is experiencing rapid growth, driven by several key macroeconomic factors. As per World Economic Forum, the country's population is projected to reach 1.515 billion by 2030, with urbanisation accelerating the demand for electricity. Notably, India's per capita electricity consumption has surged to 1,460 kWh in 2024-25, which is estimated to reach 2,000 kWh by 2030 and 4,000 kWh by 2047.
For the year 2035-36 India has set 
an ambitious electricity generation target of 3596 billion units, reflecting a 95% increase from the 1,848 billion units generated in the 2025-26. The 2025-26 generation mix includes 1,307 billion units from thermal power, 175 billion units from solar power, 167 billion units from large hydro power and 55 billion units from nuclear.
Fossil Fuel based plants, 
primarily fueled by coal and lignite, now account for 249 GW of installed capacity, making up 46.8% of the total generation capacity. Meanwhile, non-fossil fuel sources, such as renewable energy and nuclear power, contribute 283 GW of installed capacity.
In India, rural average daily supply 
increased from 12.5 hours in FY 2013-14 to 22.6 hours in FY 2024-25, while urban areas also saw improvement, with daily average supply rising from 22.1 hours to 23.4 hours over the same period. This highlights significant progress in the reliability and reach of the country’s electricity infrastructure.
Round-the-clock (RTC) tariffs 
for power in the Day Ahead Market (DAM) for FY 2025-26 are set at ₹ 3.8 per kWh, reflecting ongoing stability in the power pricing landscape
Products and consumers
Vedanta Power is strategically positioned to capitalise on the expanding power market. With operational merchant thermal power capacity of 4.2 GW, the company is 5
th largest private 
thermal player. Key assets include Talwandi Sabo Thermal Plant (1,980 MW), Sakti Thermal Plant (600 MW operational, 600 MW in Project), Meenakshi Energy (1,000 MW) and Jharsuguda Thermal Plant (600 MW).
Talwandi Sabo Thermal Plant and 
Jharsuguda Thermal Plant have entire capacity tied up to PSPCL and GRIDCO respectively with fuel linkage secured for reliable PPA power supply. In FY 2025-26, Vedanta Power operationalised 1-,000 MW of Meenakshi Energy and 600 MW (out of 1,200 MW) of Sakti Thermal Plant in Q2FY 2025-26. Vedanta Power secured 500 MW medium-term PPA with TNPDCL, of which Meenakshi Energy secured 300 MW and Sakti Thermal Plant secured 200 MW. The mix of Merchant and PPA power supply in these newly commissioned units provide Vedanta Power with a blend of secured revenue and maximisation of market rates.
Vedanta Power secured 5.34 million 
metric tonnes of linkage coal for the new assets, Meenakshi Energy (2.64 million metric tonnes) and Sakti Thermal Plant (2.7 million metric tonnes).
MEL is strategically located near to 
Krishnapatnam Port and is designed to operate with a blend of imported and domestic coal. In recent times, due to fluctuating imported coal cost and supply uncertainty, MEL is transitioning to accommodate higher domestic coal consumption with minimum technical modifications. This transition to domestic coal will ensure that MEL benefits from both domestic and imported coal based on optimal costing. To achieve higher domestic coal consumption in MEL, there is capex investment based on internal and expert study.
Talwandi Sabo Thermal Plant 
cofired 5.21% biomass in FY 2025-26 improving local livelihood and supporting India’s decarbonisation agenda.
Sakti Thermal Plant is in close 
proximity to coal mines thereby supporting competitive cost of generation. Sakti Thermal Plant Unit 2 of 600 MW is expected to be synchronised in H2FY 2026-27 and thereby commission full capacity of 1,200 MW by 2027.

Zinc
Market Overview
In FY 2025-26, the zinc price 
stayed buoyant, touching peak of US$ 3,487 per tonne, the highest level since February 2023, and averaging at US$ 2,970 per tonne, a 3% Y-o-Y increase. The rally was supported by tight physical inventories and strong consumption in galvanising and infrastructure segments, alongside rising geopolitical concerns and a weakening dollar.
In CY 2024-25, global zinc demand 
surged by 0.6% Y-o-Y to 13.66 Mnt, driven by rapid urbanisation, renewable energy (RE) transition, and structural consumption drivers in end-use markets. In China, the demand was weighed down by weak real estate, partially offset by growth in automotive and appliances. Europe witnessed 2% consumption growth as auto production stabilised despite sluggish construction. In the US, steady steel mill utilisation, tariff developments, and firm non-residential construction supported galvanised steel demand, with a potential upside from continued steel and auto sector momentum.
Market Outlook
Galvanising is the dominant zinc application, accounting for 60% of the total use driven by its critical role in construction, transport, and infrastructure. These diverse and critical end-uses reinforce zinc’s relevance and resilience across economic cycles.
India remained a major global 
driver of zinc demand, with consumption rising from 814 kt in CY 2024 to 851 kt in CY 2025, supported by broad industrial and infrastructure growth. This was reflected in the India Manufacturing Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI), averaging around 58 in CY 2026, and Index of Industrial Production (IIP), peaking in December 2025 with a growth of 7.8%, translating into higher demand for galvanised steel, zinc alloys, castings and chemicals.Government programmes such as Gati Shakti and the National Infrastructure Pipeline, along with strong steel and cement demand, continue to sustain galvanising requirements across transport, power, housing, and utilities. Road and rail modernisation alone generates a large part of the demand for galvanised steel structures.
Recently, energy transition 
investments, including in solar and wind installations, power grid expansion, and transmission towers, have emerged as significant drivers of galvanised steel structures. Simultaneously, rising auto and appliance production continue to boost demand for galvanised structures and zinc die cast components, with emerging applications in zinc-based batteries and specialised zinc products. Favourable trade dynamics and new export opportunities are further reinforcing India’s role as a strategic zinc supply hub, supporting smelter throughput and domestic availability.
Market Outlook
As per Wood Mackenzie, global zinc demand in CY 2026 is expected to grow at 1% Y-o-Y to 13.80 Mnt, supported by marginal increases in China, stabilising European consumption, and a stronger US steel linked demand. Mine supply is expected to remain tight, with output projected to fall by 4.1% Y-o-Y to 12.39 Mnt due to significant production cuts and the absence of major new project additions, resulting in consistently low treatment charges. Prices are forecast to average at c.US$ 3,064 per tonne in CY 2026, supported by low refined stocks and a softer US dollar, before gradually easing towards US$ 2,800 per tonne from CY 2026-27 onwards as refined stocks accumulate due to increased utilisation of China’s new smelting capacity.
Over the medium term, the global 
mine output is expected to plateau by CY 2028 and begin declining from CY 2029 onwards as the pipeline of advanced stage projects remains thin.India and Southeast Asia are expected to account for the bulk of incremental demand for refined zinc. With India targeting 300 Mnt of crude steel capacity by 2030, aligned with the National Steel Policy and long-term sectoral growth plans, the domestic zinc demand is forecasted to grow proportionately. This provides a strong foundation for our ambitious growth plan to double capacity.
Company Overview
Hindustan Zinc, the world’s largest integrated zinc producer and India’s only primary zinc manufacturer, held a 74% domestic primary market share in FY 2025-26 with 600 kt of domestic zinc sales. Value-Added Products (VAP) stood at 184 kt, contributing to c.22% of total sales. Around 70% of refined zinc was sold within the domestic market, while 30% was exported to South East Asia, the Middle East, the US, and Europe.
We continued to progress towards 
our ambition of 100% online price discovery (OPD) sales, achieving 95% OPD sales in FY 2025-26. The launch of Zinc Moolya, a rupee-linked live pricing module in January 2026, further enhanced price transparency and simplified transactions for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs).
FY 2025-26 marked a breakthrough 
year for commercial scaling of EcoZen, Asia’s first low carbon zinc brand with a carbon footprint of less than 1 tCO
2e 
per tonne. We signed Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs) with Tata Steel and Silox India Limited and delivered EcoZen, reinforcing efforts to accelerate its adoption across galvanising operations.
We signed MoUs with CMR Group 
and Tripura Group to operationalise manufacturing units at our upcoming Zinc Park in Khankhala, Rajasthan. These collaborations represent a key step towards building India’s first integrated downstream hub for zinc based industries that is scalable, efficient and sustainable, supported by assured raw material linkage and long-term offtake commitments. This initiative will help attract new investments, foster MSME growth, generate local employment, and accelerate Make in India manufacturing near our operations at Chanderiya, Dariba and Debari.

Lead
Market Overview
Lead prices softened during 
FY 2025-26, averaging at US$ 1,954 per tonne and settling below US$ 1,900 per tonne. This was due to adequate supply in the market rather than weakening demand. In CY 2025, global refined lead production increased by 1% to 14.35 Mnt, while primary mine output increased by 3.4% to 4.44 Mnt.
In CY 2025, global refined lead 
demand surged by 0.5% Y-o-Y to 14.24 Mnt. This was mainly driven by strong automotive battery demand across both original equipment manufacturers and replacement markets, expansion in stationary battery applications across data centres, telecom and grid storage, and robust growth in Asia.Lead demand continues to be anchored in starting-lighting-ignition (SLI) and auxiliary batteries across global internal combustion engines (ICE) and hybrid fleets, as well as energy storage and backup power applications. Factors like rising hybrid registrations in Europe, regulatory tightening on low voltage lithium ion batteries in China, and sustained growth in two- and three-wheeler mobility and telecom/backup power applications in India continue to reinforce its demand. Its recyclability of over 95% makes enhances its sustainability profile, while its role in enabling cost-effective, large-scale energy storage supports RE integration and global energy security.
Market Outlook
India’s total lead consumption for FY 2025-26 stood at 1.36 Mnt, majorly driven by batteries, cables, and galvanisers, etc. Indian lead demand is supported by batteries for automotive and energy applications, with overall consumption increasing due to its wider use in SLI batteries, cable sheathing, and PVC stabilisers. It also finds application in sectors like defence systems, telecommunications, railways, logistics, and industrial backup power.
Global refined lead demand 
is projected to grow steadily by 2.2% Y-o-Y to 14.56 Mnt in CY 2026, supported by stable automotive and stationary battery applications. China’s refined lead demand is expected to reach 6.34 Mnt in CY 2026, supported by strong new energy vehicle (NEV) related battery exports and industrial use. Against this, the global primary mine output is expected to shrink by 4.1% Y-o-Y to 4.25 Mnt with limited new project additions keeping concentrate markets tight.
Company Overview
Hindustan Zinc strengthened its position as India’s leading lead producer, increasing its domestic primary market share to 90% in FY 2025-26, up from 74% in FY 2024-25. This was supported by long-term contracts with large battery manufacturers in India, which secured a stable and consistent offtake. Over 80% of our refined lead production, translating into 157 kt was sold domestically, with 50 kt in exports. The production was focussed on 99.99% purity lead ingots, registered with the London Metal Exchange, with efforts underway to optimise sales mix towards 100% domestic consumption by securing new customers and enhancing lead applications.
Silver
Global demand and supply
Silver prices rallied to record 
highs during FY 2025-26, touching historic highs of US$ 118.45 per toz in January 2026, and averaging US$ 53.09 per toz, up 75% Y-o-Y. This spike was driven by record exchange traded product (ETP) inflows, record tight market conditions, and heightened tariff and policy uncertainty in the US. Further, strong physical/investment demand that re routed metal into US vaults while tightening availability in London, a compression of the gold-to-silver ratio below 72, and its new designation as a US critical mineral led to strategic stockpiling.
Silver demand is being structurally 
redefined by high-growth sectors such as AI infrastructure, 5G, and EV components. These emerging applications, alongside India’s massive bullion imports of over 6,000 tonnes outstripped industrial substitution efforts. As a result, industrial fabrication hit a new all-time high of c.700 Moz, offsetting the decline in photovoltaic demand caused by aggressive thrifting as manufacturers reacted to silver's price surge.Global mine output remained stagnant at 813 Moz due to declining ore grades and operational challenges across mines. The market recorded its fifth consecutive deficit of 95 Moz in CY 2025 as total supply rose by only 1% Y-o-Y to 1,022 Moz, while demand reached 1,117 Moz. This persistent shortfall has resulted in a cumulative five-year deficit of over 820 Moz, severely depleting above-ground inventories.
Indian demand
India’s silver demand reached an exceptional high of 7,000 MT in CY 2025, underscoring the country’s position as the largest consumer of silver globally, with usage driven across industrial, investment, and fabrication sectors.
Domestic markets experienced 
notable tightness throughout CY 2025 due to strong technology linked consumption (solar manufacturing, EV production, electronics, and semiconductor), festive buying, and heavy investor accumulation. This resulted in periodic physical shortages as demand consistently outpaced available supply, while positioning silver as an essential material in India’s clean energy and high tech growth story.
Investor behaviour shifted 
dramatically towards silver, with buyers accumulating metal even at record high price levels. ETF inflows, bar and coin purchases, and minimal scrap selling highlighted strong confidence and created sustained upward pressure on physical demand.
Outlook
Global silver supply is forecasted to reach a decade high of 1.05 billion ounces in CY 2026, up 1.5% Y-o-Y, driven by a surge in recycling and a modest rise in mine output to 820 Moz. While Mexico remains the leading producer, a long-term decline towards 186 Moz is anticipated by CY 2029 due to maturing legacy assets.
 •Total global demand remains structurally high but increasing diversified. While high prices may lead to thrifting and substitution in solar and electronics, yet this is expected to be offset by a 20% jump in physical investment and emerging industrial uses.
 •The outlook is defined by a persistent physical tightness, as the market enters its sixth consecutive year of structural deficit, projected at 67 Moz. It sustains an optimistic environment where the metal’s dual role as a safe-haven hedge and a critical technology mineral has established a significantly higher price floor compared to previous years.
Company Overview
Hindustan Zinc is the only primary silver producer in India and is amongst the top 10 silver producers globally. Over the past two decades, we have delivered a remarkable 20x growth in silver production, and its contribution towards overall profitability increased to c.45% in FY 2025-26. We showcased a robust sales performance of 627 MT in FY 2025-26, with 100% sales in the domestic market.

Iron ore
Market Overview
The global iron ore market 
remained resilient during FY 2025-26, supported by steady steel production and sustained infrastructure investments across major emerging economies. While China's steel demand continued to face structural headwinds from the prolonged correction in its property sector, demand across India, Southeast Asia and other developing markets remained robust, helping offset weakness in mature economies.
According to the World Steel 
Association, global steel demand is expected to bottom out and return to modest growth, supported by public infrastructure spending, manufacturing investments and easing financial conditions. Developing economies, particularly India, continue to be the key drivers of steel consumption growth.Iron ore prices remained volatile during the year, largely influenced by Chinese economic stimulus measures, inventory movements and global supply dynamics. Benchmark seaborne iron ore prices broadly traded around the US$ 90–110 per tonne range, reflecting the balancing effect of softer Chinese steel demand and resilient consumption across emerging markets.
Market Outlook
The medium-term outlook for iron ore remains constructive. Global steel demand is expected to gradually recover, supported by infrastructure-led growth, manufacturing investments and energy transition-related projects. While excess steelmaking capacity and trade-related uncertainties continue to pose challenges globally, India is expected to remain the most significant source of incremental steel and iron ore demand.With sustained investments in roads, railways, urban infrastructure, renewable energy and industrial manufacturing, India is expected to play an increasingly pivotal role in shaping global steel and iron ore markets over the coming decade.
Company Overview
The Company has solidified its position as a key player in the production of iron ore and pig iron, serving the steelmaking, construction, and infrastructure industries. With a strategic focus on optimising its mining operations, the Company has achieved significant production milestones. Sesa Goa is one of the largest private sector exporters of iron ore in India. Our total iron ore saleable production through IOK and IOG Mines is 6.5 million DMT, 5% up Y-o-Y. Pig iron production is at the highest levels with 895 kt production in FY 2025-26.
Steel
Market Overview
India further strengthened its 
position as the world's second-largest crude steel producer during FY 2025-26, with crude steel production reaching approximately 169 million tonnes, representing growth of over 11% Y-o-Y.
Global steel markets remained 
challenged by excess capacity, weak demand in certain regions and continued exports from China. However, policy measures implemented by the Government of India helped moderate import pressures and support domestic producers. Following the imposition of safeguard measures on select steel imports, finished steel imports declined significantly during FY 2025-26, while exports recorded strong growth.Market Outlook and Drivers
India’s steel demand is projected to remain robust, supported by sustained momentum across core consuming sectors such as infrastructure, construction, housing, automobiles and engineering. The World Steel Association forecasts a 9% annual growth in India’s steel consumption through 2025 and 2026, driven primarily by large-scale public capex and accelerating urban development.
Further, the Union Cabinet’s recent 
decision to extend and restructure the Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) until December 2028 with an enhanced outlay of ₹ 8.69 lakh crore –strengthens demand visibility for DI pipes.
Company Overview
ESL Steel Limited or ESL is an integrated steel plant situated in Bokaro, Jharkhand, with a design hot metal capacity of 3.5 MTPA. Its current operating hot metal capacity is 1.5 MTPA with a diversified product portfolio of Wire Rod, Rebar, DI Pipe and Pig Iron which are sold across key sectors such as construction, infrastructure, transportation and energy.
ESL achieved hot metal production 
of 1.384 million tonnes down 3% Y-o-Y and saleable production of 1.301 million tonnes down 3% Y-o-Y primarily due to the maintenance activities in one of the furnaces and subdued demand in the DI pipe segment. Also, ESL achieved the highest-ever annual production of Billet, TMT and Wire rod in the history of ESL.
The key strategic priority remains 
increasing our hot metal capacity from 1.5 MTPA to 3.5 MTPA by FY 2026-27 and downstream expansion in further years. This strategic capacity enhancement aligns with our vision to become a high grade, low cost steel producer, operating with the highest standards of environment, health and safety, while serving India’s growing requirement for quality steel products.

Operational Review 
ZINC INDIA
The year in brief
Zinc India is the world’s largest 
integrated zinc producer and amongst the Top 10 silver producers globally. During the year, the Company achieved a record mined metal production of 1,114 kt, driven by higher ore production and improved mined metal grades. Refined metal production stood at 1,048 kt, supported by the commissioning of debottlenecking projects and the 160 KTPA roaster, including a record refined zinc output of 851 kt, up 3% Y-o-Y. Refined lead production was 197 kt, reflecting a 13% Y-o-Y decline, primarily due to prior-year pyro operations being partially in lead mode and lower plant availability. Refined silver production for the year was 627 tonnes.ESG Update
In August 2025, Hindustan Zinc achieved a historic milestone by becoming the 25
th member of the International 
Council on Mining & Metals (ICMM), and notably, the first new entrant since 2021. With this achievement, Hindustan Zinc also became the first Indian company to get this prestigious membership, a moment of great significance for both the organisation and the Indian mining industry. As ICMM represents the global benchmark for responsible mining, encompassing leadership in social performance, environmental stewardship, safety, and ethical practices, the Company’s membership marks a transformative step that positions India prominently on the global stage of sustainable and responsible mining.
Furthermore, for the third consecutive year, Hindustan Zinc 
has been recognised as the global ESG leader in S&P Global Corporate Assessment 2025, being ranked 1
st among 235 
companies globally in metals and mining sector. With an improvement in overall score to 90 out of 100, the Company also got featured in the Sustainability Yearbook 2026 amongst the top 1% most sustainable organisations globally for the ninth consecutive year.
Occupational Health and Safety 
At Hindustan Zinc, ensuring the safety, health, and well-being of our employees and business partners remains a core organisational priority. Guided by our 'Zero Harm' philosophy, we continue to strengthen systems, leadership accountability, and risk management practices to create a workplace where every individual returns home safely. However, during the year, we had two unfortunate fatalities in our operations.
Following detailed investigation, we implemented 
strong corrective and preventive measures with utmost urgency, and the learnings were disseminated across the organisation. The safety and well-being of every individual remain paramount, and these incidents serve as a reminder of the need for constant vigilance and continuous improvement. 
During the year, the Company reinforced its safety 
governance framework through enhanced risk management systems, leadership capability building, and structured engagement with employees and business partners.
A significant milestone during the year was the rollout 
of a Critical Risk Management (CRM) centric Safety Management System across operations. The CRM framework focusses on identifying high-consequence risks and ensuring the implementation of effective critical controls to prevent fatalities and serious incidents. As part of this programme, five additional critical risks were launched during FY 2025-26, including risks related to Heavy Earth Moving Machinery (HEMM) fire, ventilation failure, corrosive substances and acids, excavation hazards, and exposure to hazardous gases, strengthening the organisation’s ability to proactively manage high-risk operational scenarios. 
Implementation of the CRM framework has significantly 
strengthened safety monitoring and reporting. During the year, CRM inspections were conducted across operations to ensure the effectiveness of critical controls. Additionally, Safety Action Plans (SAPs) were developed during FY 2025-26, ensuring systematic closure of identified safety gaps. Hazard and Operability Studies (HAZOP) were also conducted across all units to identify emerging risks and strengthen preventive measures.
To further strengthen leadership capability in safety, we 
conducted S.A.F.E. (Safety Awareness for Excellence in Leadership) Workshops for 42 employees, including 33 Hindustan Zinc employees and 9 business partners. These workshops were designed to enhance frontline leadership capability, strengthen risk ownership, and reinforce behavioural safety practices across operations. Six one-to-one coaching sessions have been completed for 10 identified leaders for strengthening leadership accountability and enhancing safety culture to drive behavioural change.
We also initiated a Safety Culture Survey pilot at 
Chanderiya Lead-Zinc Smelter, aimed at understanding workforce perceptions, identifying improvement areas, and strengthening the safety culture across operations. Complementing this initiative, focussed Safety Action Meetings were conducted with HEMM operators and engineering teams to address and prevent hand injuries related to HEMM operations.
Business partner engagement remained a key focus area 
during the year. We conducted Business Partner CEO Connect sessions, creating a platform to reinforce safety accountability, strengthen partnerships, and align business partners with Hindustan Zinc's safety standards and expectations. We also launched the Mine Safety Assurance Programme, aimed at strengthening safety governance in mining operations through structured assurance mechanisms, periodic reviews, and enhanced oversight of risk controls.
The Company continues to invest in strengthening 
infrastructure safety through the Infrastructure Inframatrix framework, addressing critical infrastructure risks and enhancing operational reliability.
The Company conducted Quantitative Exposure Assessment 
(QNEA), PPE fit assessments and ergonomic studies. As a result, 42 high-exposure zones were successfully converted into green zones.

Environment 
As part of Hindustan Zinc's Sustainability 2.0 movement, ambitious, globally benchmarked sustainability goals were set for FY 2029-30, which were built onto the baseline of FY 2019-20. The Company's Science Based Targets include a commitment to 50% reduction in absolute Scope 1 and 2 GHG emissions and further reduction of 25% of absolute Scope 3 GHG emissions by FY 2029-30 from the base year FY 2019-20 and further achieving net-zero emissions across the value chain by FY 2049-50.
As part of our ongoing 530 MW round-the-clock renewable

2e per

In FY 2025-26, as part of our commitment to green logistics, 
we signed two MoUs with Greenline Mobility Solutions Limited to accelerate decarbonisation of supply chains. The first marks India's first such commercial-scale initiative of deploying 100 electric vehicle (EV) trucks with battery swapping for concentrate movement between mines and smelters. The second adds liquified natural gas (LNC) trucks to our finished goods logistics fleet, doubling our LNG capacity, advancing cleaner, more sustainable logistics. Hindustan Zinc, in collaboration with Enviiiro Wheels Mobility Pvt Ltd., has flagged off first 10 EV bulker trucks at Zinc Smelter Debari, resulting in total 20 EV trucks for interunit transport of goods.
Our other initiatives in reducing our Scope 3 emissions 
include deploying 3 battery-electric vehicles (BEVs) in our underground operations at Sindesar Khurd Mine, as well as deployment of 180 LNG-powered trucks in partnership with Greenline, for upstream & downstream transportation.
We have effluent treatment plants (ETPs) and water 
treatment plants (WTPs) at all our operations which recycle processed water, which is then reused in operations making the Company maintain its zero liquid discharge. The most recent addition is water treatment plant at Rampura Agucha Mine. We have two operational dry tailing plants (DTP), one at Zawar Mines and one at Rajpura Dariba Mine, each of which recirculate more than 80% of the process water present in tailings.
We ensured effective waste management practices 
during the year, with the fumer technology at Chanderiya continuing its ramp-up to recover lead and silver cake from jarosite. The implementation plans are under place, and implementation is under progress at all sites.

These collaborations aim to enhance the viability of zinc-based batteries for a sustainable energy future.

Operations
FY 2025-26 recorded the best-ever mined metal production 
of 1,114 kt compared to 1,095 kt in the prior year driven by higher ore production, improved mined metal grades, and operational efficiencies. For the full year, ore production was 16.6 million tonnes, 2% up Y-o-Y, supported by higher output at Rampura Agucha, Zawar and Kayad Mines. 
Refined metal recorded the second-highest volume in 
FY 2025-26 at 1,048 kt, almost in line with FY 2024-25. Refined zinc production was 851 kt, up 3% Y-o-Y, supported by commissioning of smelter debottlenecking projects and the 160 KTPA roaster. Refined lead production was 197 kt, down 13% Y-o-Y, mainly due to prior-year pyro operations being partially in lead mode and lower plant availability.

In FY 2025-26, zinc prices showed periods of strength on 
the London Metal Exchange (LME), supported by tightening concentrate markets and improved investor sentiment. Global refined zinc production reached 13.85 MT (+4% Y-o-Y) in CY2025 while consumption increased to 13.66 MT (+0.6% Y-o-Y). Concentrate tightness intensified through the year, pushing spot treatment charges down, significantly pressuring smelter margins. Despite weak construction demand globally, moderate improvements in industrial activity, particularly in China’s auto sector and India’s infrastructure push, supported overall metal demand. As a result, zinc prices averaged at US$ 2,970/t in FY 2025-26, up 3% higher than FY 2024-25.
Global refined lead demand increased to 14.24 MT (+0.5% 
Y-o-Y) in CY2025; refined lead production increased to 14.35 MT (+1% Y-o-Y). Global primary mine output increased to 4.44 MT (+3.4% Y-o-Y). Lead prices remained relatively softer in FY 2025-26, averaging at US$ 1,954/t and settling below US$ 1,900/t.
During FY 2025-26, silver prices advanced sharply, 
supported by expectations of monetary easing in the US, heightened geopolitical risks and tightness in the physical market. Investment participation strengthened alongside steady industrial demand from electronics and power infrastructure supply chains. Prices touched a historic high of US$ 118.45 per troy ounce in January 2026 and averaged at US$ 53.1 per troy ounce in FY 2025-26, reflecting a 75% year-on-year increase. With limited new mine capacity additions and structurally higher industrial consumption, market sentiment for silver remained constructive.
Its outlook is defined by a persistent physical tightness, as 
the market enters its sixth consecutive year of structural deficit. It sustains an optimistic environment where the metal’s dual role as a safe-haven hedge and a critical technology mineral has established a significantly higher price floor compared to previous years.

The global refined zinc demand is showing signs of improvement around the world with major momentum gains expected to be driven by the Asian economies. A pickup in global manufacturing activity and increased investments by Chinese authorities are expected to back this momentum.
In case of global zinc supply, if the existing delays in the 
major mine projects sustain, it can result in a continued tight concentrate market, impacting the refined metal production, which would also be impacted by profitability-related and environment-related smelter suspensions across the globe.
In CY2025, LME warehouse stocks trended downward, 
falling from 141 kt to 115 kt, with the year's highest level of 195 kt recorded in April 2025. Meanwhile, SHFE stocks moved in the opposite direction, increasing from 72 kt to a high of 149 kt.
The market has faced a persistent deficit driven by supply-
side constraints, with stocks dropping to critical levels. This deficit is expected to persist into FY 2026-27, driven largely by supply side constraints and intensified further by the current conflict in the Middle East. This tightness is underpinned by historically low visible inventories, persistent concentrate scarcity, and constrained mine supply. Although supply pressures may ease modestly toward the end of FY 2026-27 as new capacities ramp-up, overall market tightness will continue to define the near-term outlook.
India’s manufacturing PMI stood at 53.8 in March 2026, 
indicating sustained expansion in manufacturing activity, while the global manufacturing PMI improved to 51.3, marking its second-highest level since June 2022. According to industry data, India’s crude steel production increased by 10.4% to 164.9 MT during CY2025, significantly outperforming global trends and reflecting strong domestic demand momentum. In contrast, global crude steel production declined by 2.0% to 1,849.4 MT over the same period.
India’s economic outlook remains robust, with real GDP 
growth estimated at ~7.6% in FY 2025-26 and projected in the range of 6.4%-6.9% in FY 2026-27 as per various estimates. Steel demand in India is expected to remain among the strongest globally, with finished steel demand projected to grow by 5-7% in FY 2026-27, supported by continued public capital expenditure and infrastructure development. This growth is underpinned by the FY 2026-27 Union capex outlay of ₹ 12.2 lakh crore, along with sustained investments under large scale programmes such as the National Infrastructure Pipeline, rail and road expansion, and urban infrastructure initiatives. Consequently, India is expected to become the world’s third-largest zinc consumer by 2030, driven by rising galvanisation demand from the construction and automobile sectors.

Hindustan Zinc has driven exploration with an aim to add new resources, upgrade existing resources into reserves category and expand its overall R&R base. This strategy supports the company’s goal of achieving a 2x growth in operations. The Company has established a dedicated exploration subsidiary named ‘Hindmetal Exploration Services Pvt Ltd (HESPL)’, a NABET-accredited Category-A exploration agency in the mineral sector and currently all exploration initiatives are being driven by this agency.
The Company has undertaken initiatives to enhance 
reserves and resources within the leasehold areas. Accelerated technology adoption, technical competence and innovative operational approaches play key roles to improve exploration performance. New prospective targets were identified along with optimally designed drill holes to examine the continuity of mineralisation.            
In line with previous years, the Mineral Resource is 
reported on an exclusive basis to the Ore Reserve, and all statements have been independently audited by SRK (UK).
On an exclusive basis, Hindustan Zinc’s total Ore 
Reserves and Resources (R&R) stood at a record 468.6 million tonnes at the end of FY 2025-26. Ore Reserves amounted to 219.1 million tonnes, net of depletion of 16.6 million tonnes during FY 2025-26, while Mineral Resources totalled 249.5 million tonnes. The contained metal within Ore Reserves is estimated at 10.7 million tonnes of zinc, 3.3 million tonnes of lead, and 350.8 million ounces of silver. Mineral Resources contain approximately 10.8 million tonnes of zinc, 4.4 million tonnes of lead, and 426.0 million ounces of silver. At current mining rates, the robust R&R base supports metal production visibility for more than 25 years.
In addition to the existing zinc-lead-silver mining 
leases, the Company is actively pursuing exploration opportunities for the three earlier acquired critical mineral blocks – namely Tungsten in Andhra Pradesh, Potash in Rajasthan, and Rare Earth Elements in Uttar Pradesh. They are aimed at expanding and diversifying its mineral portfolio in critical minerals, positioning it as a future-ready multi-metal energy transition. Company has received the Letter of Intent (LoI) for all 3 blocks and is now working towards completing other regulatory approvals, post which the focus will be on completing the exploration in three years. 
In addition to the above, currently, nine exploration 
projects of different commodities including Gold, Copper, Nickel-Chromium-PGE’s, Tungsten, Cobalt, Manganese, Vanadium and Graphite are being managed under Hind-metal Exploration Services Private Limited (HESPL) across 7 states of India. Strategic Priorities and Outlook 
Our primary focus remains on enhancing overall output, cost efficiency of our operations, diversifying our portfolio, disciplined capital expenditure and sustainable operations. With the optimistic global economic outlook for Hindustan Zinc, our goals over the medium term remain unchanged.
Our key strategic priorities include
 •Maintain a portfolio of mines with long life through continuous mineral resource addition and upgradation of the ore reserves through continuous exploration and active acquisition of new blocks of base metals and critical minerals 
 •Disciplined capital investments in organic and inorganic expansion of capacities with ramp-up of underground mines and smelters towards their design capacity, delivering enhanced metal and silver output
 •Sustain cost of production within the range of US$ 1,000 per tonne through efficient ore hauling, higher volume and grades and higher productivity through ongoing efforts in automation and digitisation, further supported by increasing share of renewable energy
 •Building a diversified product portfolio while expanding the share of our value-added products in alignment with the evolving needs of the customers
 •Continued focus on participating in auction of the critical minerals blocks by Government of India as part of the long-term objective of becoming a multi-metal energy transition enterprise
 •Progressing towards sustainable future with continued efforts towards reduction in greenhouse gas emissions, water stewardship, circular economy, biodiversity conservation and waste management, etc.
