INTERNAL FINANCIAL CONTROLS
The Board has instituted systems, policies, and 
frameworks to ensure the orderly and efficient conduct of the Company’s business, including compliance with internal policies, safeguarding of assets, prevention and detection of frauds and errors, accuracy of accounting records, and timely preparation of reliable financial information. Consistent with best practices, the ARMC and the Board regularly review the effectiveness of these internal control systems. Any identified gaps are addressed through the implementation of strengthened procedures, with such controls being reviewed periodically on an ongoing basis.
The systems/frameworks include proper delegation 
of authority, operating philosophies, policies and procedures, effective IT systems aligned to business requirements, an internal audit framework, an ethics framework, a risk management framework, and adequate segregation of duties to ensure an acceptable level of risk. Documented controls are in place for business processes and IT general controls. Key controls are tested by entities to assure that these are operating effectively. Besides, the Company has also adopted an SAP GRC (Governance, Risk and Compliance) framework to strengthen the internal control and segregation of duties/access.
The Company has documented Standard Operating 
Procedures (“SOP”) for procurement, project/ expansion management capital expenditure, human resources, sales and marketing, finance, treasury, compliance, Safety, Health, and Environment (SHE), and manufacturing.
The Group’s internal audit activity is managed through 
the Management Assurance Services (“MAS ”) function. It 
is an important element of the overall process by which the ARMC and the Board obtains the assurance on the effectiveness of relevant internal controls.
The scope of work, authority and resources of MAS 
are regularly reviewed by the ARMC. Besides, its work is supported by the services of leading international accountancy firms.
The Company’s system of internal audit includes 
covering monthly physical verification of inventory, a monthly review of accounts and a quarterly review of critical business processes. To enhance internal controls, the internal audit follows a stringent grading mechanism, focussing on the implementation of recommendations of internal auditors. The internal auditors make periodic presentations on audit observations, including the status of follow-up to the ARMC.
VIGIL MECHANISM
The Company has established a robust and transparent vigil mechanism through its Whistle-Blower Policy, which ensures that concerns relating to integrity and ethical conduct are reported and addressed in a fair, confidential, and independent manner. Complaints are reported directly to the Director – Management Assurance, who operates independently of the business management, and are supported by a global-standard infrastructure, including dedicated email IDs, a centralised database, a 24×7 multilingual hotline, and a secure web-based portal administered by an independent third party. This framework ensures anonymity, accessibility, and impartiality in the reporting process. All complaints are thoroughly investigated and resolved within a reasonable timeframe. Only substantiated cases are escalated to the Group Ethics Committee for decision-making, with periodic updates provided to the ARMC to strengthen oversight and accountability.
The details of this mechanism are disclosed in the 
Corporate Governance Report and the Whistle-Blower Policy is available on the Company’s website at  
www.vedantalimited.com , this mechanism reflects 
the Company’s zero-tolerance approach to unethical practices and its unwavering commitment to transparency, accountability, and ethical governance.The Company’s Internal Financial Control (“IFC”) framework is commensurate with the size, nature and complexity of the Company’s operations and is based on the criteria aligned with the requirements of the Companies Act, 2013. Through the IFC framework in place the Audit & Risk Management Committee and the Board also gains assurance from the management on the adequacy and effectiveness of Internal Controls over Financial Reporting (“ICOFR ”).
In addition, as part of their role, the Board and its Committees routinely monitor the Group’s material business risks. Due to the limitations inherent in any risk management system, the process for identifying, evaluating, and managing the material business risks is designed to manage, rather than eliminate risk. Besides it created to provide reasonable, but not absolute assurance against material misstatement or loss.
Since the Company has strong internal control systems 
which are further strengthened by periodic reviews as required under the Listing Regulations and ICOFR compliance by the Statutory Auditors, the CEO and CFO recommend to the Board continued strong internal financial controls.
There have been no significant changes in the Company’s 
internal financial controls during the year that have materially affected or are reasonably likely to materially affect its internal financial controls, other than as mentioned in the “Audit Report and Auditors” section to this report.
Any system of disclosure controls and procedures 
are subject to inherent limitations, including the risk of human error and the potential for circumvention or override of controls. As a result, even well-designed and effectively operating disclosure controls and procedures can provide only reasonable, not absolute, assurance regarding the achievement of their intended objectives. Further, in designing and evaluating these controls and procedures, management necessarily exercises judgment in balancing the costs of implementing specific controls against the benefits expected to be derived therefrom.
Further, the ARMC annually evaluates the design and 
operating effectiveness of the Company’s internal financial controls framework, with a focus on both assurance and continuous improvement. The framework comprises integrated policies, procedures, and systems that enable orderly and efficient operations, adherence to Company policies, safeguarding of assets, prevention and detection of frauds and errors, accuracy and completeness of accounting records, and the timely preparation of reliable financial information.

DIGITAL INNOVATION & CYBERSECURITY
CYBER SECURITY
The Group has established a robust and structured cybersecurity framework to uphold the highest standards of information security across all Business Units (“ BU”).
Each BU is led by a Chief Digital and Information Officer (“CDIO ”), a senior executive with expertise in Information 
Technology and Cybersecurity. This leadership structure ensures that cybersecurity remains a strategic priority. CDIOs, together with the respective BU Chief Information Security Officers (“ CISOs”), are responsible for overseeing 
the implementation of appropriate controls and measures to mitigate risks and safeguard critical digital assets.
To proactively address emerging cyber risks, the Group 
undertakes an annual cybersecurity review with support from information security professionals from leading global firms, including the Big Four. These reviews assess the effectiveness of our existing cybersecurity infrastructure, identify potential vulnerabilities, and guide necessary improvements. Observation coming out from assessment has been regularly reported along with remediation status or mitigation controls as applicable to management committee/leadership.
Additionally, we perform regular Vulnerability Assessments 
and Penetration Testing (“VAPT”), executed by seasoned cybersecurity experts. These rigorous assessments simulate real-world cyberattacks to identify weaknesses before they can be exploited, ensuring the integrity and resilience of our systems.
The Group’s commitment to cybersecurity extends beyond 
regulatory compliance. As the digital threat landscape evolves, we proactively review and enhance our strategies and controls to mitigate emerging risks. CDIOs are accountable for continuously monitoring and adapting our cybersecurity posture, ensuring sustained readiness to address evolving challenges.

Vedanta’s operating model and forms an integral part regulatory matters which are related to our business in a

The assessment is based on objective parameters including qualifications, experience, skills, industry knowledge, independence, and professional and functional expertise, while ensuring that the selection process remains free from any bias or discrimination on grounds such as gender, nationality, race, ethnicity or any other such factor.
The Policy also establishes the guiding principles for 
determining remuneration of Directors, KMPs and SMPs, with an emphasis on fairness, performance alignment and long-term value creation. In addition, it provides a structured framework for Board familiarisation, diversity, performance evaluation and succession planning, thereby supporting effective leadership continuity and governance.

In accordance with the provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 (“ Act”) and the Investor Education and Protection Fund (“IEPF 
/ Fund”) (Accounting, Audit, Transfer and Refund) Rules, 2016 (“ IEPF Rules ”), as amended from time to time, the company is 
required to transfer the following to IEPF:
 •Dividend amount that remains unpaid/unclaimed for a period of seven (7) years; and
 •Shares on which the dividend has not been paid/claimed for seven (7) consecutive years or more.
Additionally, pursuant to Rule 3(3) of IEPF Rules, in case of term deposits of companies, due unpaid or unclaimed interest 
shall be transferred to the Fund along with the transfer of the matured amount of such term deposits.
Your Company, in its various communications to the shareholders from time to time, requests them to claim the unpaid/
unclaimed amount of dividend and shares due for transfer to IEPF established by the Central Government. Further, in compliance with IEPF Rules including statutory modification(s) thereof, the Company publishes notices in newspapers and sends specific letters to all shareholders whose shares are due to be transferred to IEPF, to enable them to claim their rightful dues.
Basis the continuous efforts of the Company, a total of 346 investor claims have been released from IEPF till 31 March 2026 
aggregating to 4,08,461 shares.

SIGNIFICANT & MATERIAL ORDERS PASSED BY THE 
REGULATORS OR COURTS OR TRIBUNALS
Provided below are the significant and material orders which 
have been passed by any regulators or courts or tribunals against the Company impacting the going concern status and Company’s operations in the future.Copper Division
The Company had filed a Special Leave Petition before the 
Hon’ble Supreme Court against the order of Division Bench of Madras High Court vide which the Court had upheld the closure of the Copper Smelter Plant at Thoothukudi. The Hon’ble Supreme Court on 29 February 2024 concluded that the Special Leave Petition did not warrant interference under Article 136 of the Constitution of India and dismissed the Special Leave Petition filed by the Company.
The Company filed a review petition against the order passed 
by the Hon’ble Supreme Court, which has been dismissed and the Company is currently exploring all possible legal avenues including filing of Curative petition.
Further, the Company submitted its Green Copper Proposal 
to the State Government. However, as the State Government did not take any action on the proposal, the Company filed a writ petition before the Hon’ble Madras High Court seeking directions from the High Court for considering its proposal for production of Green Copper at the site instead of the earlier copper plant. The matter was listed on 18 December 2025 wherein the High Court directed the Company to file an application before the appropriate authorities and directed the State to consider the same. On the basis of the said directions of the Madras High Court, the Company filed fresh CTO Application before Tamil Nadu Pollution Control Board (“TNPCB”) which has been rejected. The Company has filed a fresh writ before the Hon’ble Madras High Court challenging the rejection order. The matter is currently pending.

Annual Report on Corporate Social Responsibility Activities for FY 2025-26
1 Brief Outline on CSR Policy of the Company
A. POLICY OBJECTIVE
  Vedanta Limited ("VEDL " or "the Company") is 
committed to creating sustainable value through responsible business practices that uphold the highest standards of ethics, environmental stewardship, and social responsibility. Recognising the importance of fostering inclusive growth and strengthening community well-being, the Company seeks to positively contribute to the economic, social, and environmental development of its areas of operation. This Policy provides the overarching framework and guiding principles for integrating responsible business conduct into decision-making and operations, while ensuring consistency, accountability, and compliance with applicable laws, regulations, and global best practices.
B. VEDL CSR PHILOSOPHY
  We at Vedanta Limited have a well-established history and commitment to reinvest in the social good of our neighbourhood communities and nation.
  CSR VISION
  “Empowering communities, transforming lives and 
facilitating nation building through sustainable and inclusive growth.”
 We believe, that
 •we can positively impact and contribute to the realisation of integrated and inclusive development of the country, in partnership with National and State Government as well as local, national and international partners;
 •sustainable development of our businesses is dependent on sustainable, long lasting and mutually beneficial relationships with our stakeholders, especially the communities we work with; •beyond government forging partnerships with corporates and civil societies/community based institutions, offer a strong multiplier for consolidating our efforts, resources towards building sustainable solutions;
 •our employees have the potential to contribute not just to our business, but also towards building strong communities.
C. THEMATIC FOCUS AREAS
  Our programmes focus on inter-generational mobility out of poverty, especially integrated development, which impacts the overall socio-economic growth and empowerment of people, in line with the baseline and need assessment, the national and international development agendas. The major thrust areas will be –
 a) Children’s Well-being & Education;
 b) Women’s Empowerment;
 c) Health Care;
 d) Water & Sanitation;
 e) Sustainable Agriculture & Animal Welfare;
 f)  Market linked Skilling for the Youth through Skill development initiatives;
 g) Environment Protection & Safety;
 h) Sports & Culture;
 i) Development of Community Infrastructure;
 j)  Participation in programmes of national importance including but not limited to disaster mitigation, rescue, relief and rehabilitation.
  The CSR activities are aligned to the specified activities in Schedule VII of the Companies Act. The focus areas may be modified from time to time, as per recommendations of the Board of the Company.

As per the applicable CSR Rules notified by the MCA, every company having an average CSR obligation of ₹ 10 crore or more during the three immediately preceding financial years is required to undertake impact assessment, through an independent agency, for its CSR projects having an outlay of ₹ 1 crore or more and which have been completed for not less than one year prior to the undertaking of such assessment.
In line with the above requirement, a brief outline of the 
projects for which Impact Assessment was carried out and the executive summary of the Impact Assessment Reports are given below:
Executive Summary of Impact Assessment 
Report:
Vedanta Limited remains deeply committed to its CSR 
philosophy of creating sustainable and inclusive growth by investing in community development across its areas of operation. The impact assessment undertaken highlights the Company’s strong focus on not just implementing high-scale interventions across key themes such as healthcare, education, livelihoods, community infrastructure, water & sanitation, Sport & culture and women empowerment, but also rigorously measuring outcomes and enhancing effectiveness. Through structured evaluation frameworks, Vedanta continuously monitors reach, efficiency, and long-term impact, ensuring that its CSR initiatives translate into tangible socio-economic improvements for communities. The assessment reinforces Vedanta’s approach of data-driven decision-making, accountability, and maximising social returns, thereby strengthening its commitment to delivering measurable and meaningful impact at scale.
The assessment was carried out by the Indian Institute of 
Corporate Affairs (IICA).

REPORT ON CORPORATE GOVERNANCE
Vedanta’s Philosophy on Code of Governance
Vedanta remains steadfast in its commitment to the 
highest standards of corporate governance while delivering sustained growth and operational excellence. In addition to adhering to the governance framework prescribed under the Securities and Exchange Board of India (“ SEBI”) (Listing 
Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (the “Listing Regulations ”), the Company continuously 
endeavours to enhance its governance framework by integrating best practices across all business functions.
Vedanta’s Corporate Governance reflects its core values, 
vision, mission, and the “ Seven Pillars of Vedanta. ” 
Governance is central to how we operate, influencing our actions, strategic choices, and accountability towards stakeholders, including shareholders, employees, and the communities in which we operate. This strong governance ethos underpins Vedanta’s journey towards sustained growth and long-term sustainability.
Corporate governance at Vedanta is a dynamic and 
evolving process. Through continuous enhancement of our processes and activities, we remain responsive to changing internal and external environments. Our approach is evidenced through consistent shareholder returns, recognitions, sound governance practices, and a performance-oriented work environment.
The Company’s emphasis on inclusive growth is embedded 
across its operations, influencing internal processes, governance frameworks, and business administration practices. This approach is underpinned by a strong commitment to good governance, supported by robust policies and frameworks that promote accountability and transparency.
We view corporate governance as an evolving journey 
focussed on the continuous creation of sustainable value. Supported by a robust framework for ethical business conduct, we consistently strengthen our governance standards through progressive ESG commitments, enhanced disclosures, Board independence, global best-practice alignment, and a strong emphasis on digital and technology-led operations.
We continuously challenge ourselves to raise the bar and 
set new benchmarks for the industry and our peers. Driving positive change remains integral to everything we do, with strong corporate governance serving as the cornerstone of this progress.

This ongoing focus on reflection and improvement ensures that our actions remain aligned with a singular purpose— driving long 
term stakeholder growth while respecting minority rights across all business decisions .
In addition to complying with the statutory guidelines, the Company has voluntarily adopted and evolved various practices of governance conforming to the utmost ethical and responsible standards of business. These practices reflect the way business is conducted and value is generated.
Integrated Reporting
Since its inception, Vedanta has made conscious efforts to operate and sustain its business in a manner that is responsible to all stakeholders. Every decision and action taken by the Company considers the potential impact on its relevant stakeholder groups. This approach reflects the organisation’s integrated thinking, which takes into account all resources and relationships that influence the Company’s ability to create sustained value. These resources and relationships, referred to as “Capitals” represent stocks of value that enable the Company’s operations.
In the course of its operations, the Company actively 
considers its external environment, including opportunities and challenges, the organisational strategies adopted to respond to these external factors, and the outputs and outcomes generated from its business activities. Beginning in FY 2017-18, the Company proactively started reporting its annual performance and strategy through an Integrated Report, in alignment with the content elements and guiding principles of the International Integrated Reporting Framework. The organisation has continued its integrated reporting journey, and its FY 2025-26 performance and forward-looking strategy are detailed in the current Annual Report.

Sustainability Reporting Journey at Vedanta
Your Company has been publishing the Sustainable Development Report for more than a decade now. The Report is prepared in accordance with the Global Reporting Initiative (“ GRI”) Standards: Core option and 
is also mapped to the United Nations Global Compact (“UNGC ”) principles and aligns with the United Nations 
Sustainable Development Goals (“UN SDGs ”). The Report 
serves as the Company’s Communication on Progress, outlining our approach and disclosures towards the triple bottom line principles of people, planet, and profit.
Vedanta applies its sustainability performance reporting 
criteria based on the GRI Standards including the Mining & Metals and Oil & Gas Sector Disclosures; the National Guidelines for Responsible Business Conduct framed by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (“MCA”), Government of India; UNGC principles; and standards set by International Council on Mining and Metals.For further insights into the sustainability practices adopted by your Company, the Sustainability Report can be accessed at www.vedantalimited.com .
Vedanta also produces three additional reports that disclose our ESG strategy and performance:
(i)  Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report 
(“BRSR”) , aligned to the guidelines laid down by 
SEBI. The BRSR report can be found within the Annual Report.
(ii)  Climate Action Report  aligned to the guidelines 
laid down by the Financial Stability Board. This report discloses in detail, the Company’s strategy in addressing and adapting to the impacts of climate change.
(iii)  Taskforce on Nature-related Financial Disclosure (“TNFD”) Report on Nature Related Financial Disclosures aligned to the guidelines/standards biodiversity strategy and risk management.Tax Transparency Reporting (“TTR”)
As a pioneer in transparent reporting, Vedanta has led the industry by voluntarily disclosing its tax contributions, thereby setting a benchmark for corporate accountability and ethical fiscal practices. This initiative reflects the Company’s commitment to its stakeholders by enhancing transparency around the profits earned and taxes contributed to governments across the jurisdictions in which it operates. Vedanta’s voluntary TTR provides a comprehensive overview of its direct and indirect contributions to the government through taxes, cess, duties, royalties and social security payments, demonstrating accountability and responsible business conduct. Through detailed disclosures of these payments, the report offers stakeholders clear and transparent insights into the Company’s direct and indirect government contributions, reinforcing trust and credibility in its fiscal conduct.
In this report, in addition to disclosing economic 
contributions under various tax and non-tax heads, we also provide information on our approach to tax-related decisions, specifically related to adherence to tax compliances and how we address tax complexities. The narration demonstrates our strong governance structure and internal controls, which promotes and ensures regulatory compliance, while encouraging tax efficiency in operations. The contributions, both direct and indirect in nature, are categorically provided for all the countries where we have significant operations.
Our guiding Tax Principles serve as a guidance, 
governing our decisions with integrity, transparency, and ensuring timely adherence to compliance in financial matters.The report focusses on our approach to Tax Governance and Strategy and includes the following:
 •Tax Principles;
 •Tax Risk Management framework, Control and Compliance framework;
 •Response to Stakeholder and Tax Environment; and
 •Tax Approach in our operating jurisdictions.

Board of Directors
The Board of Directors, as the Company’s highest governing authority, sets the strategic tone by providing long-term direction and overseeing value creation. In fulfilling its fiduciary duties, the Board is responsible for safeguarding shareholder interests, formulating long-term strategic objectives, exercising independent oversight and judgement, evaluating the effectiveness of the corporate governance framework, and ensuring balanced consideration of the interests of all stakeholders.
The Board actively engages with management by providing 
strategic guidance and oversight across key business matters. It plays a critical role in reviewing the Company’s strategy, monitoring performance, and assessing progress toward long-term objectives to support sustainable business success.
To enable focussed oversight and effective governance 
across specific areas, the Board has constituted various Board-level Committees and delegated defined responsibilities to them. Each Committee functions within the scope of its approved charter, which sets out its role, authority, and terms of reference, and makes recommendations to the Board as appropriate. All Statutory Committees are chaired by Non-Executive Independent Directors. Further details of the Committees are provided in the relevant sections of this report.
Board’s Role in Driving Leadership for 
Excellence and Innovation
The Board accords high priority to overseeing the Company’s 
operational performance and long-term strategic direction, with the objective of ensuring sustained growth, resilience, and value creation.Separate Role of Chairman and Executive Director(s)
The roles and responsibilities of the Chairman of the Board and Executive Director(s) have been demarcated and the positions are held by separate individuals. Further, during FY 2025-26, the Company also had a separately designated CFO and Company Secretary (“ CS”) & Compliance Officer.
To enable focussed leadership across businesses, dedicated business Chief Executive Officers (“ CEOs ”) and Chief 
Financial Officers (“CFOs ”) have been appointed, reporting 
to the Group Executive Director and Group CFO, respectively. Business performance is reviewed through structured monthly Core Group meetings. In addition, detailed business reviews are presented during quarterly Board meetings, with action points tracked and progress updates placed before the Board in subsequent meetings.
The Board proactively seeks comprehensive inputs, 
including detailed analysis, peer benchmarking, business review presentations, and status updates. Based on these deliberations, the Board provides guidance and strategic inputs to enhance business performance, execution effectiveness, and long-term strategy.
Drawing from their extensive industry experience and 
diverse backgrounds, Board members provide valuable perspectives to senior management on evolving industry trends, best practices, growth opportunities, and emerging risks impacting the Company.
Innovation and technology are recognised as key enablers 
of the Company’s sustained growth and competitiveness and form an integral part of Vedanta’s Seven Pillars. The Board actively encourages innovation and the adoption of advanced and pioneering technologies and plays a critical role in guiding innovation by embedding it within the Company’s strategic agenda, reviewing its effectiveness, and identifying opportunities to further strengthen long-term, sustainable value creation for stakeholders.Chairman
 •Leads the Board and ensures that it discharges its responsibilities effectively;
 •Develops succession plan for Board appointments for approval by the Board;
 •Identifies strategic priorities and new business opportunities to enhance shareholder value;
 •Promotes the highest standards of integrity, probity and governance;
 •Chairs the Board meeting and facilitates active engagement of all Directors;
 •Oversees the Director’s induction, performance and ongoing development; and
 •Engages with Company’s stakeholders to ensure that an appropriate balance is maintained between various interests.Executive Director
 •Leads the management team;
 •Develops and executes the corporate strategy in conjunction with the Board;
 •Implements the decisions of the Board and its Committees;
 •Develops Group policies and ensures effective implementation; 
 •Enhances shareholder value and implements the organisation’s vision, mission, and overall direction.
Senior Management
 •Develops and executes business strategy; and
 •Manages day-to-day decisions and ensures that decisions are in parity with the long-term objectives and policies of the Company.

Reaffirming our commitment to inclusion and care, Vedanta enhanced its Parenthood and Childcare Policy to provide holistic support to women, LGBTQIA+ employees, and all caregivers. The policy is anchored in the belief that motherhood is not a career hiatus but a phase of personal and professional growth.
Key features include flexible work arrangements, 
sabbatical leave, expanded adoption leave for primary and secondary caregivers, and gender-neutral childcare support. This progressive policy strengthens gender equity, supports employee wellbeing, and fosters a nurturing workplace environment.
Gender Reaffirmation & Leave Policy
Vedanta acknowledges and respects the unique needs and rights of transgender individuals. In line with our commitment to equality and non-discrimination, we introduced the Gender Reaffirmation & Leave Policy, providing financial, medical, and wellbeing support during the gender reaffirmation process.

Appointments
The Board comprises of experienced and qualified 
professionals with an appropriate mix of skills, expertise and competencies, enabling them to contribute effectively to the Board and its Committees. With the support of the Nomination and Remuneration Committee (“ NRC”), the 
Board periodically reviews the composition of the Board and its Committees, along with succession planning, diversity, inclusion and remuneration-related matters.
The NRC seeks to maintain a balanced and effective 
composition of the Board and its Committees, with a progressive approach to renewal over time. In discharging its responsibilities, the NRC regularly evaluates the structure, size and composition of the Board and its Committees, taking into account factors such as skills, experience, independence and diversity, to ensure alignment with the Company’s strategy. The NRC recognises that diversity and an inclusive culture are key enablers of sustainable business success and is committed to fostering a leadership team that brings together varied perspectives and constructive challenge to support effective decision-making and risk management.
The Company believes that a diverse Board enhances 
the quality of deliberations by drawing on differences in perspectives, regional and industry experience, cultural and geographic backgrounds, age, gender and professional expertise. This includes competence across areas such as finance, global business, information technology, mergers and acquisitions, governance, Environmental, Social and Governance (“ESG”), risk management, cybersecurity and other relevant domains, thereby strengthening the Company’s competitive position.
As part of the appointment process, a comprehensive 
mapping of potential candidates is undertaken through inputs from reputed search firms, senior leadership and industry advisors. Based on this mapping, candidates are assessed on parameters including qualifications, experience, domain expertise, relevance to the Company’s business, ability to contribute to long-term growth and complementarity with existing Board members and are thereafter recommended by the NRC to the Board for consideration.
The Company believes that an effective Board combines 
continuity with refreshment, leveraging the institutional knowledge of long-serving Directors alongside the fresh perspectives of new appointees. The overall objective is to ensure that the Board’s composition reflects the scale, complexity and global nature of the Company’s operations.Process for Selection and Appointment of New Directors:
The criteria for nominating a candidate for directorship has been provided for in the NRC Policy of the Company which can be accessed at www.vedantalimited.com .

The Company has a structured induction process for newly inducted directors, designed to provide an overview of the Company’s vision, values, operations, organisational framework, challenges and risk profile. Ongoing familiarisation is ensured through regular updates on regulatory and industry developments provided through formal reporting processes.

Succession Planning
Succession Planning is critical to the success of the 
Company as it ensures continuity and sustainability of corporate performance. It involves a process that recognises, develops and retains top leadership talent and further helps in identifying key roles and mapping out ways to ensure the organisation has the right people with the right blend of skills, aptitude, expertise and experiences, in the right place and at the right time. As per the NRC Policy of the Company, the NRC has laid a succession plan outlining the process for retaining, developing, and/or appointing the Board of Directors, KMPs and SMPs of the Company and it reviews such plans on an annual basis and recommend revisions, if any, to the Board.
Leadership Succession Planning:The NRC works with the management and follows the below process for effective succession planning:
1.   Identification of key critical positions 
across businesses;
2.   Assessment of potential employees and creation of a leadership pool;
3.   Development of the talent pool through actions such as involvement in strategic meetings, leadership workshops with top management, coaching, anchoring, job rotations, role enhancement, council memberships and involvement in cross function projects etc.
Processes to avoid Conflicts of Interest for 
Directors/KMPs/SMPs
The Board has established a clearly defined framework for 
disclosure of interests and related matters in compliance with the provisions of the Act and the Listing Regulations. Each Director, KMP and SMP is required to disclose any actual or potential conflict of interest at the first Board meeting held during the financial year and intimate any changes thereto on an ongoing basis. Such disclosures are placed before the Board and noted at the subsequent Board meeting, as applicable. The Board reviews and considers such disclosures to determine the appropriate course of action. Directors having an interest in a matter abstain from participating in the discussions and from voting on such matters, thereby ensuring fair, objective and unbiased decision-making.
Independent Directors
The Independent Directors of the Company meet the definitions and eligibility criteria laid down under the under the Act and the Listing Regulations.Objective:
1.  Strong leadership team 
- with right people in right roles.
2.  Develop Top Talent for future leadership roles.
3.  Robust leadership pipeline - 3 successors for all key positions.Approach:
1.  Talent Management Framework.
2.  Identify and prioritise business-critical 
leadership roles.
3.  Identify and nurture high-potential talent for leadership development.
4.  Designate "Ready Now" successors for immediate leadership needs.
5.  Plan for successors who will be "Ready in 1-2 years" and "Ready in 3-5 years."Outcomes:
1.  Prepared successors who are 
capable of stepping into leadership positions proactively, even before vacancies arise.
2.  A future-proof workforce that is well-equipped to excel in evolving business environments.
3.  Enhanced organisational stability and resilience, ensuring long-term success.
Based on the disclosures submitted by all Independent Directors and the Board’s assessment, the Board confirms that they satisfy the conditions of independence prescribed under the Act and the Listing Regulations and remain independent of the management.

Meeting of Independent Directors
Pursuant to Regulation 25 of the Listing Regulations and Schedule IV of the Act, read with the Rules framed thereunder, the Independent Directors of the Company are required to convene at least one meeting in a financial year in the absence of Non-Independent Directors and members of the management.
At such meetings, the Independent Directors deliberate 
inter alia on the performance of the Company, key risks and exposures, adequacy and timeliness of information flow to the Board, progress on projects, strategic initiatives, governance and compliance matters, Board composition and movements, human resource aspects, and the performance of the Non-Independent Directors as well as the Board as a whole.
In addition, the Independent Directors also held separate 
discussions with the Statutory Auditors to deliberate on significant accounting matters, identified risks, the internal control environment and to obtain their overall observations and feedback.
The outcomes of these meetings, along with any 
recommendations or actions arising therefrom, are communicated by the Independent Directors to the Committees concerned and the Board for consideration and appropriate action.
During FY 2025-26, the Independent Directors met without 
the presence of the management on 16 March 2026, under the chairmanship of Mr. Dindayal Jalan.

Corporate Governance comprises a framework of systems, principles and practices aimed at ensuring that the affairs of the Company are conducted with transparency, accountability and fairness, and in a manner that safeguards the interests of all stakeholders. The Board firmly believes that an effective corporate governance framework is underpinned by integrity, ethical conduct and accountability at all levels of management.
The Board recognises that a structured performance 
evaluation exercise is an important governance tool, as it provides valuable insights to Directors on enhancing their individual and collective effectiveness, leadership contribution and overall Board performance.
The NRC has laid down criteria for evaluation of the 
performance of the Directors, including Independent Directors. The evaluation framework, developed in compliance with applicable laws, regulations and guidelines, covers parameters such as attendance and preparedness, understanding of the Company’s business, quality of participation and communication, contribution to strategic thinking, domain knowledge, adherence to the Code of Conduct, and alignment with best practices and benchmarks established by global peers.
In line with the practice followed in the previous years, 
the Board evaluation was conducted with the assistance of an external third-party expert through a secure online questionnaire-based process. The evaluation framework was designed to be comprehensive yet pragmatic, with a focus on facilitating meaningful discussions, reviewing progress against areas identified in the previous evaluation, and identifying opportunities to further strengthen the effectiveness of the Board and its processes, as outlined below:
Tailored questionnares prepared by external agency and confirmed with the chairperson of NRC;Secure online platform for providing the responses;Results of the evaluation compiled by the external agency without involvement of the management;Sharing of evaluation results; andOutcome and feedback discussed at the Seperate Meeting of Independent Directors, NRC, and Board Meeting and Action Plan is agreed.

Board and Executive Leadership Remuneration 
Policy
The Remuneration Policy is significant in ensuring that 
competitive and impartial rewards are linked to key deliverables and are also in line with market practices and shareholders’ expectations.
The NRC ensures that remuneration policies and practices 
are framed and intended to attract, retain and encourage the Executive Directors (“ ED”) and the senior management 
group, while simultaneously meeting the delivery of the Group’s strategic and business objectives. The NRC further ensures the interests of the EDs and the senior management group are aligned with those of shareholders, to build a sustainable performance environment.
Remuneration Components:
The Executive Directors’ remuneration has two components: fixed pay and annual variable pay including stock incentives (performance linked incentive). The fixed component is based upon the industry practice and benchmarks considering the experience, skill, knowledge and job responsibilities. The performance linked incentive is linked to the achievement of the Company and individual performance goals. Such variable compensation is ‘at risk’, and rewards performance and contributions to both short-term and long-term financial performance of the Company. The remuneration of the EDs is governed by the agreements executed with them, subject to the approval of the Board and of the shareholders in general meetings and such other approvals as may be necessary.
The Non-Executive Independent Directors are paid 
remuneration by way of commission and sitting fees. The appointment letter detailing the terms and conditions of appointment of Non-Executive Independent Directors is available on the Company’s website at www.vedantalimited.com . The Board decides the payment 
of commission within the limits approved by the members subject to the limit not exceeding 1% of the net profits of the Company. Further, it may be noted that no stock options were issued to the Non-Executive Independent Directors during the year.

Pursuant to Section 167 of the Act, a Director shall incur disqualification if he/she does not meet the minimum attendance criteria and absents 
himself/herself from all the meetings of the Board of Directors held during a period of twelve months with or without seeking leave of absence from the Board. All Directors of the Company have duly met the attendance criteria during FY 2025-26.Audit & Risk Management Committee ("ARMC")
The Audit & Risk Management Committee plays a 
central role in the Company’s governance framework by providing independent oversight of financial reporting, risk management and internal control systems. The Committee is responsible for monitoring the integrity of the Company’s financial statements, reviewing the effectiveness of risk management processes, and overseeing the robustness of internal financial controls, including those relating to cybersecurity. The Committee also oversees the adequacy and effectiveness of the Company’s legal, regulatory and ethical compliance framework. In discharging its responsibilities, the Committee monitors the qualifications, independence, performance and effectiveness of both internal and external auditors, and assesses the quality and integrity of audit processes on an ongoing basis.
With effect from 06 June 2020, the Audit Committee and 
the Risk Management Committee were consolidated into a single Committee, now known as the Audit & Risk Management Committee, to enable integrated oversight of financial, operational and enterprise-level risks. The management team led by the Executive Director and the Head of Management Assurance Services (“MAS ”) operates 
as a sub-structure to the Committee and is responsible for implementing and operating the Company’s risk management framework. The management periodically presents detailed risk assessments and mitigation updates to the Committee, including semi-annual reviews of key risks.
Details of the Company’s principal risks and uncertainties, 
along with mitigation strategies, are set out separately in the Management Discussion and Analysis section of the Integrated Annual Report.
The Committee consists exclusively of Independent 
Directors, ensuring objective and independent judgement in matters relating to financial reporting and risk oversight. Members of the Committee bring diverse experience and strong expertise in finance, accounting, risk management and governance. In carrying out its oversight responsibilities, the Committee engages closely with management, internal auditors and the Statutory Auditors, and may seek external expert advice where considered necessary. The management remains responsible for the preparation, presentation and integrity of the Company’s standalone and consolidated financial statements, compliance with applicable accounting standards and regulatory requirements, and the establishment and maintenance of effective internal control systems. M/s S.R. Batliboi & Co. LLP , Chartered Accountants (FRN: 301003E/E300005), the Statutory Auditors of the Company, conduct an independent audit and express an opinion on the true and fair view of the financial statements.
The Committee’s agenda covers a broad range of matters, 
including review of quarterly and annual financial results, accounting policies and significant judgements, internal and external audit observations, related party transactions, inter-corporate loans and investments, and the effectiveness of internal control and risk management systems. Through these deliberations, the Committee provides assurance to the Board on the integrity of financial reporting and the adequacy of the Company’s governance and control framework.

Common Online Dispute Resolution (“ODR”) 
Mechanism
SEBI has introduced a Common ODR mechanism to 
facilitate online resolution of all kinds of grievances / disputes/complaints arising in the Indian Securities Market. The said ODR Portal permits the shareholder(s) an additional mechanism to resolve the grievances/complaints/disputes as mentioned below:
Level 1: Approach RTA or the Company
At the initial stage, all grievances/disputes/complaints are required to be directly lodged with the RTA/the Company. The shareholder(s) may send an email to einward.ris@kfintech.com /comp.sect@vedanta.co.in 
or send the physical correspondence addressed to M/s. KFin Technologies Limited (Unit: Vedanta Limited), Selenium Tower B, Plot No.: 31 & 32, Gachibowli, Financial District, Nanakramguda, Serilingampally, Hyderabad-500 032, Telangana.Level 2: Escalate to SEBI SCORES Platform
In case the grievances/disputes/complaints are not redressed to the satisfaction of the shareholder(s) at Level 1, then the shareholder(s) may escalate the same on the SCORES Platform at https://scores.sebi.gov.in/ in 
accordance with the process laid out therein.
Level 3: Initiate Dispute Resolution Process on 
ODR Platform
In case the grievances/disputes/complaints of the 
shareholder(s) are not resolved at Level 1/Level 2, then the ODR Process may be initiated through the ODR Portal at https://smartodr.in/login within the applicable timeframe under law.

The ESG Committee assists the Board in monitoring material ESG risks and overseeing the Company’s ESG strategy. The Committee meets twice a year and is chaired by an Independent Director, and includes participation from executive Directors and select KMPs, supporting effective alignment between Board oversight and management execution.
In FY 2025-26, the Board’s oversight was centered on 
material issues critical to the Company, such as workforce safety, decarbonisation and the management of carbon-related risks, supply chain management, effective oversight of tailings facilities, and sustained compliance with environmental regulations.
The Board has noted steady progress in the development 
of a comprehensive ESG governance, performance and monitoring framework. In line with the Group’s ambition of “Transforming for Good ”, the Board regularly reviews 
updates on progress across all nine ESG aims, with particular focus on the priority areas highlighted above. The Board also monitors trends in the Company’s ESG ratings, recognising that assessments by agencies such as MSCI, Sustainalytics and S&P have a bearing on the Group’s reputation and access to capital. In this context, the Board has acknowledged the Group’s efforts in establishing and strengthening VEDAS, a digital-first sustainability training platform aimed at achieving 100% employee coverage over a three-year period.
While the Board-level ESG Committee has taken note of the 
reduction in fatal incidents across the Group’s operations, ensuring safe and healthy working conditions continues to remain a key priority. The Committee seeks regular updates on the implementation of learnings from past incidents, outcomes of assessments conducted under the Critical Risk Management programme, and progress on infrastructure and system-led improvements to prevent workplace injuries.

** Non-operational UnitCommodity Price Risk or Foreign Exchange Risk 
and Hedging Activities
Fluctuation in commodity prices
Impact: Prices and demand for the Group’s products 
are expected to remain volatile/uncertain and strongly influenced by global economic conditions. Volatility in commodity prices and demand may adversely affect our earnings, cash flow and reserves.
Mitigation:  Our Group has a well-diversified portfolio, which 
acts as a hedge against fluctuations in commodities and 
delivers cash flows through the cycle. We consider exposure to commodity price fluctuations to be an integral part of our Group’s business and its usual policy is to sell its products at prevailing market prices, and not to enter into long-term price hedging arrangements. However, to minimise price risk for finished goods where price of raw material is also determined by same underlying base metal prices (e.g. purchase of alumina, copper concentrate for manufacturing and selling copper and aluminium products, respectively) we employ back-to-back hedging. In exceptional circumstances, we may enter into strategic hedging with prior approval of the EXCO. The Group monitors the commodity markets closely to determine the effect of price fluctuations on earnings, capital expenditure and cash flows.
Currency exchange rate fluctuations
Impact: Our assets, earnings and cash flows are influenced by a variety of currencies due to the diversity of the countries in which we operate. Fluctuations in exchange rates of those currencies may have an impact on our financials. Although the majority of the Group’s revenue is tied to commodity prices that are typically priced by reference to the US dollar, a significant part of its expenses are incurred and paid in local currency. Moreover, some of the Group borrowings are denominated in US dollars, while a large percentage of cash and liquid investments are held in other currencies, mainly in the Indian rupee. Any material fluctuations of these currencies against the US dollar could result in lower profitability or in higher cash outflows towards debt obligations.
Mitigation:  We do not speculate in forex. We have developed 
robust controls in forex management to monitor, measure 
and hedge currency risk liabilities. The Committee of Directors reviews our forex-related matters periodically and suggests necessary courses of action as may be needed by businesses from time to time, and within the overall framework of our forex policy.
Exposures on foreign currency loans are managed 
through the Group wide hedging policy, which is reviewed periodically to ensure that the results from fluctuating currency exchange rates are appropriately managed. The Group strives to achieve asset liability offset of foreign currency exposures and only the net position is hedged. The Group uses forward exchange contracts, currency swaps and other derivatives to hedge the effects of movements in exchange rates on foreign currency denominated assets and liabilities. The sources of foreign exchange risk are outstanding amounts payable for imported raw materials, capital goods and other supplies as well as financing transactions and loans denominated in foreign currencies. The Group is also exposed to foreign exchange risk on its net investment in foreign operations. Most of these transactions are denominated in US dollars. Short-term net exposures are hedged progressively based on their maturity. A more conservative approach has been adopted for project expenditures to avoid budget overruns, where cost of the project is calculated taking into account the hedge cost. However, all new long-term borrowing exposures are being hedged. The hedge mechanisms are reviewed periodically to ensure that the risk from fluctuating currency exchange rates is appropriately managed.

SEBI has vide its order dated 19 May 2021 imposed 
a penalty of ₹ 5 crore on erstwhile Cairn India Limited (merged with Vedanta Limited in 2017) under Section 15HA of SEBI Act for violation of Regulation 3(a), (b), (c), (d), Regulation 4(1) and 4(2)(k) and (r) of SEBI (Prevention of Fraudulent and Unfair Trade Practices) Regulations, 2003 and a penalty of ₹ 25 lakhs under Section 15HB of SEBI Act for violation of Regulation 19(1)(a) of SEBI (Buyback) Regulations, 2003 for not completing the buyback offer in the year 2014. Vedanta Limited filed an appeal against the Order before the Securities Appellate Tribunal (“ SAT”) 
contending inter alia that it cannot be conclusively proved that Vedanta Limited made such misleading announcement in relation to a buyback of its shares. Pursuant to its order dated 5 October 2023, SAT set aside the Order (“ SAT Order”). SEBI has filed an 
appeal before the Supreme Court challenging the SAT Order. The arguments have been concluded, judgment awaited.

which empowers a holistic approach to Health, Safety, Environment, and Sustainability by providing a central platform to manage all critical functions. Currently, all ESG related data are getting logged in Enablon and assurance of the same is also conducted in this integrated software. All incidents/ UA/UC are also logged in Enablon across the Group and this platform helps ensure timely closure of the same by sending notifications to respective users. Multiple reports and dashboards are configured and circulated to help users identify areas of concern and track data closure. During the year, we have gone live with a total of nine modules till date. Currently around 12,000 users are mapped in the portal which includes employees and business partners as well.
Employee Sensitisation-Ethics and Governance
Awareness through Video Clips and Mailers – In alignment with the Company’s zero-tolerance stance on unethical practices, employees are regularly sensitised on critical ethical topics such as Prevention of Sexual Harassment (“ POSH ”), anti-bribery, conflict 
of interest, gift policy, anti-corruption, ESG, etc. through engaging short video clips and informative mailers, fostering a more ethical and inclusive workplace every day.
Ethics Quiz – To assess the awareness and 
understanding of employees on ethical standards, Company conducts periodic Ethics quizzes.
Ethics Compliance Month – As part of its annual 
initiative, the Company conducts an Ethics Compliance Month wherein awareness and training sessions are conducted covering governance and critical internal policies including POSH, prevention of insider trading, anti-bribery, anti-corruption, anti trust regulations etc.
Insider Trading Monitoring Portal
Online Gift Declaration Portal
The employees can neither accept nor send gifts/
entertainment in exchange of any business/services/giving off any confidential information etc.to derive any benefit conflicting with the interest of the Company.
The Company has in place an online gift declaration 
portal to ensure transparency, with employees required to promptly declare all gifts received in line with the Gift Policy forming part of the Code of Business Conduct and Ethics.
Statutory Compliance System
In order to ensure best-in-class compliance monitoring and reporting, the Company has in place an internal standard operating procedure ("SOP") to manage statutory compliances across all businesses and a top of the line automated compliance management system with regular updates on checklists of all applicable statutory requirements. The SOP has been revised to reduce subjectivity and enhance uniformity with an objective criticality matrix and robust reporting mechanism.
As a best practice, it is mandatory for all CEOs to 
issue and sign-off on compliance certificates for their respective businesses each quarter for placing before the Audit & Risk Management Committee and Board.
Release of Climate Action Report
The Company published its sixth Climate Change 
Report for FY 2025–26, outlining the Group's decarbonisation strategy and climate-related disclosures in alignment with the recommendations of the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures ("TCFD"), while also incorporating selected elements of the International Financial Reporting Standards (" IFRS") 
S2 framework.
Building on this foundation, the Company intends 
to publish a Climate Action Report for FY 2026–27, aligned with both the TCFD recommendations and the IFRS S2 framework. The report will provide a comprehensive account of Vedanta's climate strategy, progress, and pathway towards achieving Net Zero emissions by 2050 or sooner and will be made publicly available on the Company's website.
The Climate Action Report will complement the 
Company's broader ESG disclosure suite, including the GRI-based Sustainability Report, Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report ("BRSR "), TNFD 
disclosures, and the Integrated Report. Through these disclosures, the Company aims to provide stakeholders with transparent, comprehensive, and decision-useful information on its climate-related risks and opportunities, sustainability performance, and long-term value creation strategy.
UPSI Sharing Database
The Company also has an online UPSI sharing 
database where time stamp of UPSI shared by employees is maintained digitally. The full access of this UPSI database is only restricted with the Compliance Officer.

9.  Does the entity have a specified Committee of the Board/ Director responsible for decision making on sustainability related issues? (Yes / No). If yes, provide details.The Board of Vedanta Limited has constituted key committees to oversee sustainability, governance, and compliance, ensuring alignment with its strategic priorities. The principal committees include:
ESG Committee : The Board-level ESG Committee oversees all sustainability and ESG matters. It works 
closely with the Corporate Sustainability and ESG function to drive and monitor initiatives under the 
Transforming for Good agenda. The Committee is appointed by the Board, chaired by a Non-Executive Director, and includes at least one Independent Director. The Group HSE & Sustainability Head and ESG Director are permanent invitees.
Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) Committee : The CSR Committee supervises the Company’s 
CSR initiatives, recommends the annual CSR plan and resource allocation to the Board, and reviews 
performance against approved plans.
Audit and Risk Management Committee : This Committee oversees financial reporting, internal controls, 
and risk management frameworks, including cybersecurity. It monitors strategic, operational, financial, 
sustainability, and compliance risks, and evaluates the performance and independence of auditors.
Stakeholders’ Relationship Committee (SRC): The SRC focusses on stakeholder engagement, ensuring 
timely resolution of shareholder grievances, improving shareholder experience, and overseeing registrar and shareholding-related matters.
For additional information on the roles and responsibilities of the above-mentioned Committees and 
their members, please refer to the Corporate Governance section on page 322  of the Integrated Annual 
Report FY 2025–26.

4.  Does the entity have an anti-corruption or anti-bribery policy? If yes, provide details in brief and if available, provide a web-link to the policy.
  Yes, Vedanta is committed to conducting business with the highest standards of integrity, transparency, and accountability. This commitment is embedded in its Code of Business Conduct and Ethics (COBCE), which establishes a zero-tolerance approach to bribery and corruption and also addresses key areas such as conflict of interest, confidentiality, anti-trust, insider trading, and whistle-blower protection. The Code of Business Conduct and Ethics (COBCE) is available on the Company’s website (Click here).
  The Anti-Bribery and Anti-Corruption (ABAC) framework forms an integral part of the COBCE and is aligned with applicable laws, including the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 (India), the UK Bribery Act, 2010, and the U.S. Foreign Corrupt Practices Act, 1977.
  The COBCE is supported by a set of enabling policies and guidance documents, including the Insider Trading Prohibition Policy, Anti-Trust Guidance Notes, Supplier Code of Conduct, and Whistle-Blower Policy.
  A formal vigilance mechanism is in place to enable both internal and external stakeholders to report concerns, supported by structured investigation and resolution processes. All employees and Board members are required to periodically affirm compliance with the COBCE. This is reinforced through regular training programmes covering the Code of Business Conduct and Ethics and ABAC principles, ensuring 100% employee co verage.

2. (a) Does the entity have procedures in place for sustainable sourcing?
  Yes, Vedanta Limited has established structured procedures for sustainable sourcing across its value chain.
   Sustainable procurement is governed through the Company’s Supplier Code of Conduct (SCOC) and Supplier 
Sustainability Management framework, which are mandatory for all suppliers, vendors and contractors. These frameworks set clear expectations across key areas including human rights, labour standards, occupational health and safety, environmental management, business integrity and anti-corruption.
   Critical and high-risk suppliers are subject to risk-based due diligence, including third-party assessments where applicable, to evaluate compliance with regulatory requirements and sustainability standards. Suppliers are required to adhere to applicable human rights laws and, where relevant, commit to the principles of the Modern Slavery Act.
   Environmental stewardship is a core component of supplier expectations, requiring responsible resource use, emissions management, and waste-handling practices across supply chains. Vedanta also mandates ethical business conduct, zero tolerance for bribery and corruption, and the establishment of grievance redressal mechanisms for supplier employees and stakeholders.
   Capacity-building initiatives and internal training programmes support procurement teams in embedding sustainability considerations into supplier selection, onboarding and performance monitoring processes, ensuring continuous improvement and alignment with responsible sourcing objectives

3.  Describe the processes in place to safely reclaim your products for reusing, recycling, and disposing at the end of life, for (a) plastic (including packing) (b) e-waste (c) hazardous waste and (d) other waste.
  This indicator is not applicable to Vedanta Limited, as our business primarily operates on a B2B model, supplying our products as raw materials to various industries. However, Vedanta’s waste management philosophy is rooted in its Waste-to-Wealth commitment. While end of life product reclamation is not relevant to our core operations, circular economy principles are deeply embedded across our value chain, focussing on minimising waste disposal, maximising resource efficiency, and converting process residues into value added materials.
 Governance Framework
  All business units are governed by Vedanta’s Technical Standard on Resource Use and Waste Management, aligned with the Basel Convention, ICMM Principles, and IFC Performance Standards. Waste management is structured around the hierarchy:
 Avoid 
 Reduce  Reuse  Recycle  Recover  Treat  Dispose
  Compliance is mandated under the Hazardous Waste Rules 2016, E-Waste Management Rules, Plastic Waste Management Rules, and applicable State Pollution Control Board (SPCB) requirements. Vedanta’s long-term ambition is to achieve Zero Waste to Landfill across all operations.
 Plastic Waste
  Bulk dispatch of metals and minerals means plastic packaging is minimal. Where plastic waste arises, it is segregated at source and channelled through authorised recyclers. Notably:
 •HZL, BALCO, and TSPL operate under a strict single-use plastic prohibition
 •TSPL and Cairn hold CII Single-Use Plastic-Free certification
 •Meenakshi Energy maintains a traceable scrap yard management system
 E-Waste
  Not a material stream for core operations. All e-waste from IT, instrumentation, and administrative equipment 
is disposed of exclusively through government authorised recyclers, with full inventory tracking and recycling certification maintained. Hazardous Waste
  Classified and managed under the Basel Convention and Hazardous Waste Rules 2016. Key streams such as spent oils, refractories, spent pot lining, smelter residues are managed through a recovery-first approach:
 •Co-processing in cement kilns as an alternative fuel
 •Treatment through registered recyclers
 •Disposal at authorised TSDFs only, via SPCB approved vendors
 •Used oil re-refined through certified agencies
 Robust manifest systems ensure end to end traceability and regulatory compliance.
 High-Volume, Low-Toxicity (HVLT) Waste and Other Non-Hazardous Waste
  HVL T streams: ash, red mud, jarofix, slag, and lime grit are inherent to metals and mining operations. All are stored in scientifically engineered facilities, including tailings dams and ash dykes, under continuous geotechnical and environmental monitoring.
  Circular utilisation is prioritised over disposal. Fly ash is supplied to the cement and construction industries; slag is channelled into road construction and building materials; jarofix serves as structural fill. Red mud valorisation initiatives are currently under development. Remaining non-hazardous waste is managed through recycling, composting, and, as a last resort, scientifically managed landfill.
4.  Whether Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) is applicable to the entity’s activities (Yes / No). If yes, whether the waste collection plan is in line with the Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) plan submitted to Pollution Control Boards? If not, provide steps taken to address the same
  Yes, Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) applies to specific business units of Vedanta Limited where regulatory requirements arise, primarily for plastic packaging and related materials.
  Applicable entities including BALCO, Cairn, VAL-Jharsuguda, Sterlite Copper- Silvassa, and ESL Steel Limited, have aligned their waste-collection mechanisms with the EPR plans submitted t o the respective Pollution Control Boards. 
The waste collection plans align with statutory EPR obligations and are implemented through authorised recyclers and traceable disposal channels.
  BALCO is now formally registered as a Brand Owner under the applicable Plastic Waste Management Rules, thereby strengthening regulatory compliance and reporting transparency. The unit continues to enforce a ban on single-use plastic within plant premises and ensures that plastic waste generated within operational and township areas is channelled to authorised recyclers, including co-processing in cement plants where appropriate.
  Furthermore, all business units ensure that plastic packaging materials received, particularly for imported goods, are segregated at the source and routed for recycling through authorised agencies, in line with approved EPR action plans.

ongoing expansion.
 •Jamkhani Coal Mine:  Accessible restrooms, ramps, and wheelchairs across facilities.
 •Sterlite Copper, Silvassa: Wheelchair access at premises.

10. Health and safety management system:
 a.   Whether an occupational health and safety management system has been implemented by the entity? (Yes/ No). 
If yes, the coverage of such a system?
   Yes, Vedanta has established a comprehensive Occupational Health and Safety Management System aligned with International Council on Mining and Metals (ICMM) guidelines, International Finance Corpor ation (IFC) 
recommendations, and applicable global standards. The framework is implemented across all operations, including subsidiaries, joint ventures, associates, and acquisitions, ensuring a consistent and rigorous approach to workplace safety.   The company is committed to achieving excellence in health and safety management, with a strong focus on eliminating unsafe conditions and practices. Its operations are certified to ISO 45001:2018, reflecting adherence to internationally recognised standards.
   Governance is reinforced through a robust oversight structure, supported by the Vedanta Safety Performance Standard, which enables systematic monitoring and continuous improvement across all business units.
 b.  What are the processes used to identify work-related hazards and assess risks on a routine and non-routine basis by the entity?
   Vedanta adopts a structured and multi-layered approach to identify and manage work-related hazards across routine and non-routine activities, aligned with ISO 45001:2018 and internal risk assessment standards.
  Routine Risk Identification and Control
 •Hazard Identification and Risk Assessment (HIRA) and Job Safety Analysis (JSA) are used t o identify task-level 
risks and implement preventive controls.
 •Standard Operating Procedures are developed and periodically updated to ensure safe and consistent practices.
 •Site-level HIRA registers are maintained and regularly updated to reflect operational changes and emerging risks.
  Advanced Risk Assessment for Non-Routine Activities
 •Hazard Identification Study (HAZID), Hazard and Operability Study (HAZOP), and Quantitative Risk Assessment (QRA) are used for complex and high-risk scenarios.
 •A Permit-to-Work (PTW) system ensures that such activities proceed only after thorough risk assessment and control implementation.
 •Simultaneous Operations (SIMOPS) reviews are conducted to manage overlapping risks.
  Critical Risk Management (CRM)
 •A structured CRM programme identifies and manages critical risks across operations based on ICMM methodology.
 •Key risks include working at height, energy release, confined spaces, electrical hazards, loss of containment, vehicle pedestrian interaction, uncontrolled loads during lifting, uncontrolled release of energy, and loss of containment of molten material.
 •Controls are continuously strengthened based on incident data and risk evaluations.
  Workforce Engagement and Monitoring
 •Toolbox Talks (TBTs) are conducted regularly to communicate task-specific risks and reinforce safe practices at the worksite.
 •Safety interactions, Visible Felt Leadership visits, and Contractor Safety Field Audits support ongoing monitoring and compliance.
 •A digital platform (Enablon) enables data-driven tracking, assessments, and corrective actions.
   This integrated framework ensures proactive risk identification, effective mitigation, and continuous improvement, supporting Vedanta’s commitment to a zero-harm workplace.
 c.   Whether you have processes for workers to report the work-related hazards and to remove themselves from such risks. (Y/N)
   Yes, Ensuring a safe and responsive work environment, Vedanta has put in place robust systems that enable workers to report hazards and step away from unsafe conditions when required. The Company’s digital platform, “V-Unified”, provides a centralised channel for employees, workers, and visitors to log safety concerns, facilitating effective tracking, timely intervention, and closure. In parallel, site-level healthiness scores are continuously monitored to strengthen safety controls and drive improvements in workplace conditions.
   Proactive hazard identification is reinforced through structured safety practices such as regular safety interactions, planned hazard tours, and critical risk verification exercises across operations. These efforts are further supported by AI-enabled monitoring tools, including T-Pulse cameras, which help identify and flag unsafe acts and conditions in real time.

   Vedanta also emphasises individual accountability and empowerment by upholding the right to refuse unsafe

 d.   Do the employees/ worker of the entity have access to non-occupational medical and healthcare services? (Yes/ No)
   Yes, Most employees and workers at Vedanta are covered under comprehensive medical insurance, along with life, personal accident, and related risk coverage, providing financial protection during unforeseen events. Employee well-being is a key priority, with emphasis on sustaining physical, mental, and emotional health to support overall effectiveness and engagement.
   Vedanta maintains a strong healthcare ecosystem across its operations, including access to well-equipped hospitals at major locations with qualified medical professionals. Preventive healthcare is supported through annual medical check-ups and awareness initiatives focussed on both physical and psychological well-being. Emergency response capability is strengthened through Advanced Life Support (ALS) ambulance services at key sites, supported by trained medical responders to ensure rapid intervention in critical situations.

These services are complemented by structured wellness and stress management programmes across locations, aimed at strengthening resilience and promoting balanced lifestyles. Access to sports and fitness infrastructure further reinforces preventive health and overall well-being.

12.  Describe the measures taken by the entity to ensure a safe and healthy workplace.
  Vedanta has established a Group-wide Health, Safety and Environment (HSE) framework comprising technical standards, 
management systems and site-specific safety programmes, with “zero harm” as the overarching objective. 
  Critical Risk Management and Infrastructure
  The Critical Risk Management (CRM) programme identifies 17 critical risks based on historical incident data. Control measures have been defined for each risk and are subject to continuous monitoring at the shop-floor level by line functions. The Infra-Matrix framework is deployed across sites to map critical risks with corresponding physical safety infrastructure, including pedestrian pathways, man-machine segregation corridors, conveyor guarding and restricted-access zones.  Engineering Controls
  The Company undertook targeted interventions to eliminate or mitigate risks at source. Key initiatives include:
 • BALCO:  21 km of a 23-km man-machine segregation corridor commissioned; 2 km in progress
 •VAL–Lanjigarh: Wagon tippler installed for bauxite unloading, eliminating manual worker exposure to wagon door 
line-of-fire
 • ESL Steel:  Segregation of routes for raw material vehicles and personal vehicles to avoid interaction between heavy 
vehicle and personal vehicles
 • Athena Power: Integration of Enablon for health risk tracking to conduct risk identification and closure proactively
 •MEL Nickel:  Installation of Isolators to eliminate the need of isolation inside the group feeders to avoid direct touch of 
panel when in live
 Behavior-Based Safety and Culture
  Behavior-based safety programmes, including Visible Felt Leadership (VFL), CRM audits and Contractor Field Safety Audits, are implemented across sites to identify and address unsafe acts and conditions. Cairn Oil & Gas continues to operate a structured observation programme to maintain L TIFR and TRIFR within defined targets. ESL Steel is implementing a safety culture transformation programme (‘Prarambhik’) with external advisory support, with progressive ownership by line functions. AI-enabled surveillance systems have been deployed at Silvassa for real-time monitoring of unsafe behaviours.
  Training and Emergency Preparedness
  Mandatory safety induction is conducted for all personnel prior to site entry. Regular Toolbox Talks, Pre-Activity Briefings (PAP Talks) and Pre-Job Safety Meetings are conducted across shifts. Competency-based training is ensured prior to authorisation for hazardous operations. Emergency preparedness is strengthened through periodic mock drills conducted across locations, including ESL Steel and Fujairah. At Fujairah, remote working protocols and contingency plans were activated in response to regional developments.
  Occupational Health
  Pre-employment and periodic medical examinations are conducted for all employees and contract workers, as 
applicable. Long-term health surveillance programmes are in place at select units, supported by engineering controls for ventilation, dust and noise management. Chemical safety measures, including installation of Diphoterine stations, and occupational health risk assessments have been implemented at MEL Nickel.
  Safety Governance
  A Group-level, CEO sponsored committee oversees CRM implementation, safety infrastructure and injury prevention 
initiatives. Safety alerts issued post any fatal incident are tracked for closure of corrective and preventive actions across all business units to enable cross-functional learning and strengthen accountability.
  Through these measures, Vedanta continues to build a culture where safety is non-negotiable, embedding accountability at every level of the organisation, from the shop floor to the boardroom, and driving measurable progress towards a zero-harm workplace across all its operations and geographies.
